Title: Serian records hazardous API reading
Article:
KUCHING: Serian recorded a hazardous Air Pollutant Index (API) reading as of 8am today.
According to the Department of Environment (DOE)'s Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS) portal, the API reading at the Serian District Police Headquarters monitoring station stood at 364.
Meanwhile, three areas in Sarawak recorded very unhealthy API readings, namely Samarahan (300), Kuching (291) and Sri Aman (214).
Areas recording unhealthy API readings include Sarikei (195), Sibu (187), Bintulu (179), Samalaju (171), Mukah (170), Kapit (159), Miri (155) and the Miri Industrial Training Institute (ILP) (151).
An API reading of zero to 50 indicates good air quality, 51 to 100 indicates moderate air quality, 101 to 200 unhealthy, 201 to 300 very unhealthy, and above 300 hazardous.
API figures are updated hourly based on readings from 68 monitoring stations nationwide.

Title: Merdeka spirit opens new path for 17-year-old TVET hopeful
Article:
BUKIT MERTAJAM: A 17-year-old girl whose education was disrupted by her mother's prolonged illness and financial hardship will get a second chance after securing a place at a TVET college in Sik, Kedah.
Entrepreneur Development and Cooperatives Minister Steven Sim Chee Keong said his two adopted children, Gabriel Ooi and Sandira, helped the girl, Nabila, resume her education after she was forced to leave school when her mother fell ill and lost her income.
"Although Ooi and Sandira are of different races and religions, they stepped forward to help Nabila.
"That is the spirit of Merdeka – Malaysians standing together for a shared future," he said.
Sim said the story began two weeks ago when Ooi sent him a brief WhatsApp message asking for help.
"I initially thought he wanted help for himself. But it turned out that he and Sandira had found Nabila, a girl who had stopped going to school because her family could no longer afford it. Her mother had been ill for a long time," he said in a Facebook post.
Ooi, who had completed his studies, and Sandira, who is still studying at Universiti Utara Malaysia, then began looking for a way to help Nabila resume her education.
Sim said they found a TVET college in Sik, Kedah, that offered hostel accommodation, addressing the transportation problem faced by Nabila and her family.
"Ooi asked if I could help with the family's expenses so she could begin her studies. I simply replied: 'Jalan Teruih' (Keep going)," he added.
The Bukit Mertajam member of parliament said Nabila had been living with her grandparents since her mother fell ill four years ago and lost her source of income, forcing the family to return to their hometown.
Financial difficulties forced Nabila to leave school and fall behind in her studies.
Sim said Ooi and Sandira refused to let her circumstances determine her future and continued searching for a suitable TVET institution.
After securing Nabila and her family's agreement, they registered her at the college, where she is expected to begin her studies next week.
Sim said he had also sought permission from Nabila's mother and grandparents to take her in as his adopted child and pledged to cover her expenses until she completed her studies.
He said Nabila's grandfather was saddened by the prospect of being separated from her, but accepted that staying in a hostel was necessary for her education.
"More importantly, when Nabila succeeds, I hope she will not only be able to help her family but also become like my other adopted children – always caring and willing to lend a hand to others," he said.
With Malaysia set to celebrate its 69th Merdeka, Sim said Ooi and Sandira's actions showed that patriotism extended beyond flying the Jalur Gemilang.
"Merdeka is not just about flying the Jalur Gemilang. It is about Malaysians working together for a shared future," he said.

Title: Third victim found near two others in Kota Kinabalu fire
Article:
KOTA KINABALU: The third victim who went missing in a fire that destroyed about 200 water village homes in Numbak here was found by firefighters today.
The victim was found at 7.46am, not far from the location where the first two victims were found charred at 6.40am and 7.20am respectively during the firefighting operation.
The three victims were identified as Mohd Hasrul Abd, 4, Ana Abd, 6, and Norfadilah Mohd Thajia, 8.
They comprised two siblings and their cousin and were reported missing in the fire, which involved Kampung Lok Buta, Kampung Lok Poring and Kampung Sabang Lama.
Acting Kota Kinabalu Fire and Rescue Station chief, Senior Assistant Fire Superintendent Mohd Hannis Moktar, when contacted, confirmed the discovery of the third victim.
He said firefighters found the victim while continuing search operations and overhaul work at the fire site.
"The third victim was found not far from the location where the first two victims were found," he said.
Earlier, the fire that broke out early today destroyed about 200 water village homes in an area measuring about 79m by 116m.
The fire was brought under control at 6.26am, while the cause of the incident and extent of losses are still under investigation.

Title: #NSTViral: Malaysians head to southern Thailand despite boycott calls, travel advisory
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysians continued crossing into southern Thailand for the Merdeka Day long weekend, despite recent boycott calls and travel advisories over traffic enforcement and security concerns.
Videos and photographs shared on social media on Friday showed long queues at border checkpoints in Perlis and Kedah, with congestion particularly heavy at Padang Besar.
TikTok user Amirul Guider shared a video showing vehicles backed up at the Padang Besar border checkpoint about 7am yesterday.
"Lively today. Happy holidays, everyone," he wrote.
Threads user @nrul.fatihah_ also posted photographs showing long queues at immigration counters at about the same time.
"Update on the situation at the Padang Besar border at 7am. So many people," she wrote.
Meanwhile, a video shared in the Hatyai Travel Facebook group showed traffic congestion at the Bukit Kayu Hitam Immigration, Customs, Quarantine and Security Complex at about 8.30am yesterday.
The scenes prompted amused reactions from social media users, with some remarking on the irony of Malaysians spending the
Merdeka Day weekend
in Thailand.
Others expressed surprise at travellers' willingness to endure the long queues despite recent calls to boycott Hat Yai following complaints over alleged strict enforcement by Thai traffic police.
The calls followed a reminder from Malaysian authorities for motorists to respect the laws of other countries after several Malaysian bikers were fined in Thailand.
The cross-border movement also came despite
Malaysian authorities advising
the public to defer non-essential travel to southern Thailand following a series of coordinated attacks in Narathiwat, Pattani and Yala last week.
The attacks prompted Malaysia to tighten security along its border with Thailand.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Iceland in suspense after close EU vote
Article:
REYKJAVIK: Iceland voted Saturday in a referendum on whether to resume membership negotiations with the European Union, with a close race predicted and the final result expected late in the night or the next morning.
Voting stations closed at 10pm (2200 GMT).
In the absence of exit polls and with ballot counting only beginning once voting stations closed, it could take several hours before a clear victory emerges for the 'Yes' or 'No' camp.
The country of just under 400,000 people applied to join the EU in the wake of a 2009 financial crisis that devastated its economy.
Membership talks were then suspended in 2013 when a Eurosceptic government came to power.
An opinion poll by analyst firm Maskina on Friday gave the 'Yes' side a slight edge with 50.4 per cent of the vote, but that gap is within the statistical margin of error.
If the 'Yes' side wins, an accession agreement would be negotiated with Brussels and then put to a new referendum on actual membership.
The issue of fisheries – a pillar of Iceland's economy and over which Reykjavik wants to retain exclusive control – would have to be hammered out with Brussels, which this time around appears more willing to find "creative solutions".
On Saturday, Iceland's 273,000 voters were asked to answer 'Yes' or 'No' to the question: "Should Iceland resume accession negotiations with the European Union?"
Technically, the referendum result is non-binding, but the coalition government headed by Social Democratic Prime Minister Kristrun Frostadottir has vowed to respect the result.
"This has been a tight race, extremely exciting," she said Saturday after casting her ballot in Reykjavik.
She added that the campaign had "lifted discussions about the EU, about Iceland's place in the world, about our general geopolitical situation and status, to a higher level."
The government has called a press conference for Sunday at 1pm (1300 GMT) to present its plans going forward.
If the 'No' side wins, the government has already vowed not to resume accession negotiations during its term, which runs until 2028, and indicated that it would refer to parliament the question of a possible formal withdrawal of Iceland's EU membership bid.
Political analysts have said it is unlikely the government would resign.
'A nail-biter'
"I think for the last week there has been momentum for the 'No' side," Lovisa Olafsdottir, a 24-year-old consultant, told AFP at a referendum watch party for the 'No' camp just before voting stations closed.
"Of course it will be a close call. This will be a nail-biter, but we are hopeful that we will come out on top," said Freyr Rognvaldsson, a 48-year-old public relations employee and 'Yes' campaigner.
Throughout the campaign, debates have mainly revolved around domestic and economic issues, even if rising international tensions, with the war in Ukraine and US President Donald Trump's ambitions for neighbouring Greenland, have featured in discussions.
Iceland's economy has recovered and is now thriving.
Many see no reason to join the EU since the island is already part of the European single market through the European Economic Area, which does not cover the Common Fisheries Policy.
But Iceland's currency is volatile, and the flip side of its newfound prosperity is soaring inflation and interest rates, leaving many indebted Icelandic households glancing longingly at the prospect of adopting the euro and its lower interest rates.
On the global stage, the return of war in Europe with Russia's invasion of Ukraine has shaken established security doctrines.
Iceland is an island strategically located in the sub-Arctic. It has no military and depends on Nato and a 1951 bilateral agreement with the United States for its defence.
Trump's unpredictability and his threats to take over neighbouring Greenland – which he has mixed up with Iceland on several occasions – have added to Icelanders' concerns.
The result of Saturday's vote will be followed closely by the EU, which has not welcomed a wealthy, net contributor to its budget since 1995.
Brussels would see Icelandic membership as an example of positive enlargement that could also make it more palatable for member states to agree to take in poorer countries like Montenegro – or even help change some minds in ultra-wealthy non-EU member Norway, which could end up finding itself isolated.

Title: Two found charred, one missing in fire that destroys 200 homes in Kota Kinabalu
Article:
KOTA KINABALU: Two people were found charred while another remained missing after a fire destroyed about 200 homes in Numbak here early today.
The three victims comprised two siblings and their cousin.
Acting Kota Kinabalu Fire and Rescue Station chief, Senior Assistant Fire Superintendent Mohd Hannis Moktar, said two victims were found by firefighters during the firefighting operation.
He said the search for the third victim was still under way, while the identities and status of all three victims were being verified.
"The fire involved non-permanent water village houses across three villages — Kampung Lok Buta, Kampung Lok Poring and Kampung Sabang Lama.
"Initial estimates showed that about 200 homes were affected across an area measuring about 79m by 116m," he said.
He said the Fire and Rescue Department received an emergency call at 1.40am before fire engines arrived at the scene at 1.54am.
"The fire was brought under control at 6.26am to prevent it from spreading to nearby areas.
"Firefighting and search operations, as well as other work, are still ongoing," he said.
[[nid:1521593]]
The operation involved 44 personnel from the Kota Kinabalu, Lintas, Penampang and Tuaran Fire and Rescue stations, with assistance from the Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM) and Sabah Electricity.
Sabah Fire and Rescue Department director Mohd Pisar Aziz was also at the scene, together with state assistant director of operations, Senior Assistant Fire Superintendent I Muhammad Taqiuddin Victor Doon, and other senior department officers.
The actual number of homes destroyed is still being verified, while the cause of the fire and estimated losses have yet to be determined.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: UPTM helps Pos Kemar youth chart brighter future
Article:
GERIK: Education is key to transforming lives and giving the Orang Asli younger generation in Pos Kemar a chance at a better future.
Through the Mara Prihatin—Jejak Aspirasi UPTM @ Pos Kemar programme, Universiti Poly-Tech Malaysia (UPTM) students took learning beyond the classroom, engaging directly with children and  students in the community.
UPTM vice-chancellor Prof Dr Sharifah Syahirah Sy Shiekh said the programme gave UPTM students an opportunity to give back to the community while gaining knowledge and first-hand experience of the Orang Asli community.
"One of the values we emphasise is humanity. This programme gives our students an opportunity to go into the field, contribute to the community and understand the challenges faced by more than 5,000 Orang Asli residents in Pos Kemar.
"It is also part of our aspiration to inspire more than 1,034 students in Pos Kemar to pursue higher education and become professionals in various fields in the future," she said when met at launch of the programme recently.
The community programme was also attended by Mara chairman Datuk Dr Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki and deputy Dewan Rakyat Speaker Datuk Seri Dr Ramli Mohd Nor.
[[nid:1521588]]
Asyraf, who is also UPTM pro-chancellor, said Pos Kemar had great potential to serve as a model for nurturing promising Orang Asli students through to higher education.
He said the achievement of an Orang Asli student from Pos Kemar, who is now in the final year of medical studies at Universiti Sains Malaysia (USM), demonstrated the potential of the community's younger generation when given the right opportunities and support.
"We want to make Pos Kemar a model where promising students can be identified and nurtured, with support provided to help them progress to higher levels of education.
"Only through knowledge and education can their lives be transformed," he said.
Activities held during the community programme included an interactive early childhood education session conducted by UPTM's Bachelor of Early Childhood Education (Honours) students at Tabika Kemas Pos Kemar, involving 30 6-year-old children.
[[nid:1521587]]
Meanwhile, the UPTM Mural Project at Sekolah Menengah Kebangsaan Rancangan Penempatan Semula Kemar not only brightened the school environment but also gave students early exposure to options available to them after completing their schooling.
For UPTM, the direct involvement of its students in the community also adds value to their learning experience by allowing them to gain a better understanding of the lives and challenges faced by communities outside the campus.
Working with the community allowed them to see first-hand the realities and challenges faced by people outside the campus environment while putting their knowledge and skills into practice.
The programme also extended beyond education, with activities covering skills development, welfare and economic opportunities as part of a broader effort to support the community.
The Mara Prihatin—Jejak Aspirasi UPTM @ Pos Kemar programme is a multi-agency collaboration between UPTM, Mara and strategic partners aimed at supporting the Orang Asli community through education, human capital development, welfare, volunteerism, entrepreneurship and socio-economic development.
[[nid:1521586]]

Title: Media Prima celebrates Malaysian spirit through 'Wajah Malaysia' campaign
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Everyday Malaysians will take centre stage in Media Prima Bhd's campaign celebrating the resilience, compassion and diversity that shape the country's shared identity.
The "Wajah Malaysia: Nadi Negara, Cerita Kita" campaign will feature digital initiatives and community activities for National Day and Malaysia Day.
Its centrepiece, the 630 Wajah Malaysia Face Hunt, invites Malaysians to submit their portraits for a digital mosaic celebrating the nation's diversity.
The completed mosaic will be unveiled across Media Prima's platforms and digital screens on Malaysia Day on Sept 16.
A Wajah Malaysia roving truck will visit major national month events, including the Ambang Merdeka Festival at Dataran Merdeka from Aug 29 to 31 and Keretapi Sarong on Sept 16.
There will be celebrity appearances, live performances, interactive games, giveaways and photography opportunities.
Media Prima will also participate in the National Day parade in Putrajaya.
Media Prima group managing director Datuk Mohd Rafiq Mat Razali said National Day and Malaysia Day provide an opportunity for Malaysians to reflect on their collective identity and the values that unite them.
"Media Prima is committed to connecting people, celebrating our shared experiences and strengthening the bonds that unite us.
"Through Wajah Malaysia, we want to celebrate everyday Malaysians whose resilience, compassion and diversity define our shared identity.
"We hope this campaign reminds every Malaysian that our greatest strength has always been our people."
Media Prima group chief marketing officer Amir Rasyidi Johari said the campaign was designed to turn the celebrations into meaningful opportunities for public participation and connection.
"Whether it's contributing a portrait to the 630 Wajah Malaysia mosaic, visiting our roving truck or joining us at the Ambang Merdeka Festival, the National Day Parade or Keretapi Sarong, we want people to experience the campaign firsthand.
"By combining digital engagement with immersive on-ground experiences across Media Prima's integrated ecosystem, we're creating a campaign that reflects the spirit of Malaysia — diverse, inclusive and united."
The campaign will feature patriotic content, special programmes and community stories across Media Prima's television, radio, print, digital and social media platforms. Participate in the Face Hunt by uploading your portrait to the platform from Aug 17 to 31.

Title: The missing in Nepal-Tibet flash floods
Article:
KATHMANDU: Nearly 3,000 people were still missing on Sunday, with 682 confirmed dead after flash floods and landslides hit the Nepal-Tibet border.
The figures are likely to change, which is not uncommon in the chaos after a major disaster.
Here are the latest numbers:
In total: 2,980 missing
Nepal's disaster agency increased the total number of people missing on its side of the border to 2,426 on Saturday.
The total number of missing in Tibet is now 554, with seven people confirmed dead, China's Xinhua news agency reported early on Saturday.
Together, the total number of missing stands at least 2,980.
Nepal's disaster agency on Friday said 517 foreigners – which could include tourists as well as foreign workers – were still missing.
Chinese officials on Friday put the number of foreigners missing at 260.
Nepal's disaster agency said Saturday that at least 675 people had been killed, bringing the total to at least 682.
Nepal
The Nepal Tourism Board figures on Friday said 149 Nepali tourists were among the 622 it listed as missing.
The Nepal disaster agency put the figure lower, at 127.
It was not immediately clear how many Nepali residents of the area were unaccounted for, but the figure is believed to be in the hundreds.
China
China's foreign ministry said on Thursday that nearly 100 Chinese nationals were among the missing in Nepal.
The Nepal Tourism Board said eight Chinese were unaccounted for, but 16 had been rescued.
That was in addition to the 554 still missing on the Chinese side of the border, the state news agency Xinhua reported on Saturday.
India
Nepal's new tourism board figures on Friday showed 98 people from India were missing, but 85 others had been rescued.
United States
Ninety US citizens were missing, the State Department said Thursday, adding that three had been rescued. It said it was not aware of any US fatalities.
The Nepal Tourism Board put the figure at 65 missing on Friday, with two rescued.
Ukraine
The Nepal Tourism Board put the number of Ukrainians still missing on Friday at 61.
Ukraine's embassy in Nepal said on Friday it was aware of 62 citizens with whom contact had been lost, revising its earlier number upwards by six.
[[nid:1521570]]
Malaysia
The Nepal Tourism Board put the number at 51.
Australia
The number of Australians missing stood at 42 on Sunday.
United Kingdom
Thirty-three people from the United Kingdom were missing, the Nepal Tourism Board figures showed on Friday.
Latvia
Twenty-nine Latvians were missing, the Nepal Tourism Board said on Friday.
Canada
The Nepal Tourism Board said 25 Canadians were among the missing on Friday. Canada's foreign ministry put the figure at 30 in both Nepal and Tibet.
South Korea
The Nepal Tourism Board said Friday that nine South Korean tourists were missing.
South Korea's foreign ministry said Wednesday that it had had no news of nine hydropower workers.
Singapore
Nine Singaporeans were unaccounted for, the Nepal Tourism Board said.
Germany
Eight German citizens are missing, according to the Nepal Tourism Board.
Russia
Nine Russians are unaccounted for, while two have been rescued, the Nepal Tourism Board said on Friday.

Portugal: three, with two found safe (Portuguese government). The Nepal Tourism Board said only one Portuguese citizen was missing.

Title: Defence sec-gen takes first flight in Su-30MKM ahead of National Day flypast
Article:
news@nst.com.my
KUALA LUMPUR: Defence  Ministry secretary-general Datuk Lokman Hakim Ali got his first taste of flying in the back seat of a Royal Malay-sian Air Force (RMAF) Sukhoi Su-30MKM fighter jet during preparations for the Merdeka flypast.
Lokman said it gave him a first-hand perspective of the capabilities of the   fighter,  as well as the skills and professionalism of the people operating and supporting it.
"The experience also offered an  understanding of the capabilities required to keep  strategic assets at a high state of readiness.
He said this at the flypast rehearsal at Subang air base yesterday. The Su-30MKM Flanker is among the RMAF assets taking part in the  69th National Day celebration.
Lokman said the aircraft continued to play an important role,  particularly in protecting the country's airspace and maritime interests.
"It is not merely a high-performance aircraft. It is a combat system whose effectiveness depends on a combination of technology, personnel and  operational support," he said.
He  said maintaining the readiness of assets such as the Su-30MKM was a strategic necessity, but readiness went beyond ensuring the aircraft was in good condition.
"It also depends on pilots being able to  understand and use the capabilities of their aircraft,  making  training crucial.
"The better the pilots' understanding and skills, the greater the value and capability we can derive from a  platform.
"The RMAF has also benefited from exercises involving aircraft from different generations, including Exercise Elangaroo 24, during which Royal Australian Air Force F-35As conducted air combat training with RMAF F/A-18Ds and Su-30MKMs," he said.
These exercises, he said, allowed pilots to understand the strengths and capabilities of different platforms while enhancing interoperability.
"In real-world situations, it is not technology alone that determines effectiveness. The skills, experience and tactical judgment of pilots also play a  significant role," he said.
He said the strength of the Su-30MKM lay not only in the aircraft itself, but in the combination of its platform, pilots, engineers, technicians and  support ecosystem, including those working behind the scenes to keep the aircraft mission-ready.
"Domestic personnel with expertise in mechanical, electrical, structural and system fields work together to ensure the aircraft remains ready to carry out its missions.
"This expertise, supported by maintenance, repair and overhaul (MRO) capabilities, spare parts, weaponry and technical support, is an important part of our asset readiness."

Title: Govt reviewing egg prices, says minister
Article:
SERDANG:   The government is reviewing rising egg prices following concerns from producers about high operating costs and mounting industry pressures, said Agriculture and Food Security Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Sabu.
He said his ministry and the Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Ministry had met industry players to find out  what was causing egg prices to spike.
He said issues involving new rules by local authorities, including those to resolve fly infestation, would be raised in a meeting with   executive councillors in charge of agriculture.
"The ministry will  monitor the situation to ensure sufficient supplies while safeguarding consumers and the sustainability of the industry," he said  at the Kebun di Rumah Sendiri  campaign here on Friday.
Kuala Lumpur and Selangor Egg Merchants Association chairman Low Hin Ching said retail egg prices had risen five times over the past three weeks due  to lower yields caused by poor-quality feed and hot weather.
"When farms raise  prices by two sen, we follow  and increase ours by two sen as well."
Grade A eggs were selling at RM15 per tray of 30 at wholesale and RM15.90 at retail. Grade B eggs were RM14.70 wholesale and RM15.60 retail, while Grade C eggs were RM14.40 and RM15.30, respectively.

Title: 'This is all we know': Farmer fears 40-year-old poultry business may end
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR:  Desmond is facing a dilemma over the two poultry farms he inherited from his father, one that could bring an end to the 40-year-old family business.
Earlier this year, the two  farms in Kuala Langat, with some 200,000 birds, were shut following complaints about  fly infestation from  residents.
"The authorities told us to clean up the area.
"We were allowed to reopen  after they came to inspect and were satisfied with what they saw," he told the
New Straits Times
.
"The flies are a nuisance, but they are difficult to control because they are drawn to chicken farms, move from farm to farm and reproduce very quickly."
Desmond said flies had always been present, although the growth of  residential areas had worsened the problem.
He said flies at poultry farms, especially open farms like his, were unavoidable, although their population could be managed with traps, pesticides  and proper sanitation.
Still, the problem takes  time to resolve.
Desmond said the Veterinary Services  Department had provided guidance, but the results would not be immediate.
The bigger concern, he said, was a deadline set by local authorities for him to convert his open farms to closed-house systems.
"When we met the authorities recently, they said we would not be granted a licence for an open farm in 2½ years.
"It costs around RM60 to raise a bird in a closed-house system.
"That's about RM12 million, excluding land cost."
He said a new farm would require agricultural land to be located at least 200m from a residential area.
"We are cooperating when there are complaints, but please don't force us out in a short time."
He said taking multi-million-ringgit risks might not be feasible for many poultry farmers.
He said the authorities should give  farms more room and flexibility, while making closed-house requirements mandatory for new applicants.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Chicken, egg prices rise as poultry farms face mounting pressures [WATCH]
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Chicken and egg prices are rising as poultry farms face closure amid fly infestations, labour shortages, rising feed costs and regulatory pressure, industry players said.
The Federation of Livestock Farmers' Associations of Malaysia  said  farms could meet domestic demand, but market supply had become "very tight" amid  industry strain.
A source told the
New Straits Times
that farm closures over fly complaints had  affected production.
The closures were mainly  in Negri Sembilan, although those in Perak, Penang and Selangor had also been ordered to shut.
Penang Rural Development, Agrotechnology, Food Security and Entrepreneurship Committee  chairman Datuk Rashidi Zinol said seven farms were  closed following complaints but had since been allowed to resume operations after carrying out improvements.
The NST also sought comments from authorities in Perak, Selangor and Negri Sembilan.
The affected farms, with a combined capacity of about 3.7 million live chickens, have had their licences suspended, while a handful were fined. Some have since been allowed to reopen.
The sources said open farms, relying on natural airflow for ventilation, were the most affected.
Complaints from  communities over swarms of flies and maggots have prompted enforcement action, with some farms closed early this year still unable to resume operations.
This has been aggravated by the heatwave, a pesticide shortage and insufficient manpower.
"There are not enough pesticides in the market because some brands have not received approval. At the same time, we can't get foreign workers unless quotas to bring in more are approved," said the source.
Federation adviser Datuk Jeffrey Ng said farmers were struggling to meet enforcement standards requiring "zero-fly and zero-maggot" conditions.
"The authorities ask us to be clean so that the fly issue can be managed better. But if farms are to be managed better, we need more workers."
Ng said foreign worker quotas, set decades ago, no longer reflected operational demands.
"Some 20 to 30 years ago, worker quotas were set at one foreign worker per 8,000 chickens for open-house farms, and one worker per 20,000 chickens for closed-house farms.
"That was meant purely for routine operations. Now, when authorities expect farmers to clear manure every day or two to eliminate flies completely, we do not have the manpower  to support that level of maintenance."
The source and Ng said farmers needed clear guidelines and a mechanism to rectify problems and reopen closed farms.
"We don't have the tools and we don't have the manpower to deliver what they want, yet farms are  ordered to close. In a way, they are pushing farmers to close down and we are entering a very bad cycle," said Ng.
He said unclear procedures could leave workers stranded and prompt frustrated owners to abandon the industry.
[[nid:1521542]]
Pressure is mounting on open-farm operators, particularly in Perak, where the state government has set  until the end of this year for all  farmers to transition to closed-house systems. Open farms account for almost half of all chicken farms in the state.
The industry source said many open-farm operators were small and medium enterprises that could not easily afford the  capital needed to convert to closed-house systems.  Planning approval could also take years.
"Farmers have been asking for a compromise, but  there has been no word on that," said the source.
At the federal level,  the sources said farmers have engaged the Agriculture and Food Security Ministry, but were told  state authorities, particularly local councils, had the authority to close down farms over  fly complaints.
At an event in Serdang on Friday, Agriculture and Food Security Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Sabu said the ministry was reviewing  industry feedback.
"We take note of concerns about higher chicken and egg prices, including rising operating costs and other factors affecting the industry," he said.
Farmers are also facing rising feed costs. Ng said corn prices had risen by between 10 and 15 per cent in recent weeks because of international market pressures.
He said the industry remained dependent on imported feed, but farmers were  absorbing higher costs rather than passing them directly to consumers.
"Global price fluctuations are an ongoing risk, but chicken and egg prices in the local market remain affordable  under current free-market dynamics."
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Israel army says struck Hamas commander in Gaza hospital compound
Article:
GAZA CITY: Israel's military said it struck a Hamas commander within the compound of a Gaza hospital on Saturday, while the territory's health officials said Israeli strikes elsewhere killed four people.
It is the latest bloodshed to occur in the war-shattered territory despite a US-backed ceasefire that took effect in October 2025, with Israel continuing to target Palestinians it says are Hamas fighters.
The military said it struck a Hamas commander who "was hiding within the compound" of Al-Aqsa Martyrs Hospital in the central city of Deir al-Balah, but was unable to immediately confirm if he had been killed.
It said the commander, who it did not name, advanced "attacks against IDF troops and Israeli civilians" and was targeted in a structure adjacent to hospital buildings.
"Earlier today, Al-Aqsa Martyrs Hospital was targeted, with a small storage facility hit," the hospital's director Raed Hussein said.
"Thankfully, there were no major casualties, apart from four minor injuries," he told AFP, but said the strike had "caused extensive material damage."
AFP footage from the scene showed several damaged water tanks on the roof of a building and debris down below.
The military said steps had been taken to "mitigate the risk to civilians", adding that it had warned Gazan medical authorities two days earlier about "the cessation of the use of medical facilities for terrorist purposes."
Doctors Without Borders (MSF) said that it was "appalled by reports of an Israeli airstrike within the Al-Aqsa Hospital compound", adding that "hospitals should be safe places for patients and healthcare workers."
"At a time when Israeli forces are routinely targeting hospitals, it is of utmost importance that all parties respect and preserve the neutrality and protection of medical facilities," it wrote on X.
Gaza's civil defence agency, which operates as a rescue force under Hamas, said four people were killed in other strikes across the territory on Saturday.
Israeli fire east of Deir al-Balah killed one person, the agency said. The Israeli military said it was checking the reports.
An Israeli strike near a roundabout in the Tel al-Hawa neighbourhood of Gaza City killed two people and injured several others, the civil defence said.
When contacted by AFP, the Israeli military said it struck a "military operative" in the area.
Another strike killed one person and critically injured another in the southern city of Khan Yunis, the civil defence said. The Israeli military said it was checking the reports.
Israel has kept striking Gaza and its forces have made further inroads despite a US-brokered ceasefire announced in October, with Israel insisting it must eliminate threats from Hamas, which led the unprecedented Oct 7, 2023 attack against Israel.
Israeli operations in Gaza have killed at least 1,313 people since the ceasefire came into effect, according to the Palestinian territory's health ministry, which also operates under Hamas authority and whose figures are considered reliable by the United Nations.
The Israeli army has reported five deaths in its ranks over the same period, as well as the death of one civilian contractor.

Title: Getting the dogs, horses ready for Merdeka Day parade [WATCH]
Article:
PUTRAJAYA:  With tails wagging and hooves  trotting, the animal contingent taking part in the   National Day parade have been put through intensive training and acclimatisation.
Twenty-five  dogs from the armed forces' Military Dog Wing or "Wolf Wing" and 25 horses from the army's Ceremonial Cavalry Squadron will take part in the parade.
With  the canine and mounted contingents  nearing the final stages of preparation, the handlers said the animals were ready to take centre stage alongside their human counterparts tomorrow.
Wolf Wing assistant head Captain Duin Tat said the K9 contingent, comprising 25 handlers and 25 dogs, had undergone about a month of  preparation at the Army Combat Training Centre in Johor before arriving here  for final rehearsals.
"Our  focus is on the health and readiness of  the handlers and the dogs. Deployment requires the animals to be 100 per cent healthy. We conduct daily temperature and health checks under 24-hour veterinary supervision.
"Every dog has a different temperament — some tend to pull ahead, while others are hesitant to move. Walking alongside live assets requires strict control, which is why we train them to follow commands precisely so they do not cause disruptions during the parade," he said.
He said hot weather and haze were among the concerns during preparations, with the unit following veterinary advice to ensure the dogs remained hydrated and healthy.
For him, the most rewarding aspect of the preparation is the bonding process, as handlers adjust to the  temperaments of different dogs.
[[nid:1521534]]
Meanwhile, assistant instructor and dog handler Corporal Jhonny Mansiang said this year's parade would be his first.
Although the parade  will last  20 to 30 minutes, Mansiang said the handlers and dogs could spend about an hour waiting for their turn to march during rehearsals.
The horses had also undergone weeks of preparation to familiarise them with the equipment, route and sounds they will experience.
Staff Sergeant Mustakim Marhan Musa, 38, said the 25-horse contingent, including two backup horses, began  preparations about a month before the parade.
Mustakim, who  served in the unit for 18 years, said some horses were startled during the initial rehearsals but  became more composed by the second and third sessions.
He said controlling the animals became  challenging when they left the stables and moved towards the parade area, where they would be exposed to the  crowd and aircraft.
"Loud noises from fighter jets, helicopters and the crowd can cause the horses to panic, so handlers must work to keep them calm," he said.
Rider and groomer Corporal Mohd Shahrul Azmer Ishak, who joined  the unit in  2014, said taking part in the National Day parade remained a source of pride.
"This is my sixth time taking part in the Merdeka parade.
"It is a privilege to showcase our unit's assets to the public and spark their interest in the armed forces," he said.

Title: Norway's King Haakon VIII pays tribute to late father in first speech
Article:
OSLO: Norway's new King Haakon VIII on Saturday addressed Norwegians for the first time since taking the throne, paying tribute to his 89-year-old father who died the day before.
"Above all, you were a person who remained committed to your values and dedicated to your duties," Haakon said of the late King Harald V in a televised speech.
The new regent said it had been "deeply moving to see all the people, candles, messages and flowers filling up the Palace Square."
"We greatly mourn his loss. At the same time, it gives us consolation and strength to know that there are so many who are grieving with us," the 53-year-old said.
Visibly moved, he also noted that his father and mother, Queen Sonja, would have celebrated their 58th wedding anniversary on Saturday.
"Happy anniversary, dearest mamma," he said, choking back tears.
Flags flew at half-mast on Saturday as scores of Norwegians continued to flock to the palace, adding flowers to the masses already on the ground after more than 20,000 people paid their respects Friday.
The late king enjoyed massive support, despite the slew of scandals that dogged his family in the final stretch of his 35-year reign.
'My turn'
Haakon thanked his father for being such "a wonderful papa" to him and his sister Martha Louise, and acknowledged that "a huge task awaits me."
"He reminded our family constantly that each of us must do things in our own way. Find our own path forward. Be ourselves," Haakon said of his father.
"Now it is my turn," he declared.
Kari Lyngestad, a 45-year-old nurse, said she was moved by what she described as a very "emotional" speech.
"I'm happy and I'm sad, and I believe everything is going to be okay, we have a good new king," she told AFP outside the palace just after the broadcast.
Meanwhile, teacher Eyvind Storeheier called it a "fantastic" speech.
"I think he will be much like his father. He will be a king of the people," the 56-year-old said.
Tributes have poured in from European monarchies and world leaders, including US President Donald Trump, who hailed the memory of "a strong, proud, and greatly respected man."
Earlier Saturday, King Haakon held audiences at the palace with the leaders of the Church of Norway, parliament and Supreme Court.
He also received Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Store for a viewing of the late king's casket, which was brought to the palace from Oslo University Hospital Friday evening.
Memorial services Sunday
A national period of mourning has been declared. No date has been set for the late king's funeral.
Churches across the country will hold memorial services on Sunday. The royal family was scheduled to attend a service in Asker south of Oslo.
On Tuesday, King Haakon will swear an oath of allegiance in parliament.
City halls across Norway set out condolence books on Saturday for the public to write personal messages.
Oslo Mayor Anne Lindboe, who had called off her own wedding on Friday due to the king's death, was the first to write a message in Oslo's City Hall.
"Dear King Harald, you didn't need a crown to be a king. Thank you so much for everything you have done for our city. We will never forget you," she told reporters she had written.
King Haakon and his wife, Queen Mette-Marit, are not expected to be crowned in a ceremony – Norway abolished coronations in 1908.
But, like his father and grandfather before him, Haakon could opt for a consecration ceremony at Trondheim Cathedral, where Norwegian monarchs were crowned between 1814 and 1906.
King Harald was widely seen as the embodiment of an open and tolerant Norway, and praised for leading a monarchy that was modern and modest.
Scandals
Harald had been in hospital in Oslo since August 17, suffering from haemolytic anaemia, a condition caused by an abnormally rapid destruction of red blood cells that leads to fatigue and shortness of breath.
He faced mounting health problems in his final years, forcing him to scale back his official schedule.
The past year has been a turbulent one for the Norwegian royal family. Queen Sonja, also 89, was herself briefly admitted to hospital in May due to heart problems.
Haakon's wife Mette-Marit is under scrutiny for her ties to the late US sex offender Jeffrey Epstein.
And in June, Mette-Marit's son from a previous relationship, Marius Borg Hoiby, was sentenced to four years in prison for two rapes, a sentence he is appealing.
Mette-Marit, 53, who suffers from a serious lung disease, underwent a lung transplant in July.

Title: Peeling back the past: Secrets uncovered at KL's heritage sites
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Sometimes, the clues to a building's past are hiding in plain sight.
At Muzium Diraja Kuala Lumpur, a restoration team uncovered a double-layer roof and other construction features that differed from conventional Malaysian building methods.
At Seri Negara, peeling back layers of paint revealed an original duck egg green colour, while an old staircase was found buried beneath a pathway.
At Medan Pasar, stripping away decades of alterations exposed frescoes, Venetian-arched windows, decorative details and construction techniques that offered a glimpse into how early Kuala Lumpur was built.
For the teams restoring the three heritage sites, the work has been less about making old buildings look new and more about understanding what they were before deciding what should stay, what should go and what could be brought back.
A SECRET HIDDEN ABOVE
Kamal Engineering deputy project manager Muhammad Hanif Mohamad Sharif said the team encountered several structures that were not identified during the initial assessment.
One of the most notable was a double-layer roof, unusual for Malaysian architecture.
Hanif said the double roof appeared to have been meant to provide insulation, possibly reflecting construction practices used in other climates, including in Britain.
Built in 1929 as the residence of a wealthy Chinese businessman, Muzium Diraja was later used as a Japanese military headquarters before being acquired by the government and converted into a royal residence, later a museum.
Each phase left traces, requiring the restoration team to distinguish original features from later alterations.
Samples of timber flooring were sent to the Forest Research Institute Malaysia for analysis before replacement material was selected, while lime plaster samples from 24 points around the building were tested to determine their original composition.
Original elements were preserved, including distinctive tessellated tiles discovered beneath old carpet in the Royal Gallery.
HISTORY UNDER OUR FEET
For Seri Negara, the building itself became a source of information during its 10-month restoration, completed before its reopening in December last year.
Pengurusan Aset Warisan chief executive officer Hilme Hassan said peeling back layers of paint revealed that several colours were used in different periods, including what appeared to be the original duck egg green.
"That helped guide our decision on the colour for the restoration of the windows and door frames of the building."
Another discovery came when the team investigated the building's external steps.
Historical drawings led the team to investigate further, revealing the original steps buried beneath a pathway that was constructed later.
The team also uncovered the original stone threshold and parabolic step staircase at the main lobby.
"We were able to uncover and retain a feature that had survived for more than a century."
Historical drawings, illustrations and old photographs helped the team understand how the 113-year-old building evolved, but Hilme said the physical fabric remained the most important source of information.
The restoration also involved recovering important architectural elements, including the grand timber staircase, which had been relocated and altered during an earlier phase.
"For us, that is ultimately what conservation is about. We are not trying to make an old building look brand new. We are trying to preserve its authenticity while preparing it for the next chapter of its life."
WHEN CULTURES MELD
Medan Pasar presented a different challenge, with restoration extending beyond individual buildings to an entire historic streetscape.
Formerly known as Old Market Square, the area was among Kuala Lumpur's earliest commercial centres, developing alongside the city's growth as a trading and supply hub for the tin mining industry.
Over time, many buildings were altered, underused or left to deteriorate.
Creador Foundation co-founders Brahmal Vasudevan and Shanti Kandiah said restoration work uncovered remnants of original frescoes and facades, including Venetian-arched windows and a consistent cornice-line height across individual units.
[[nid:1521522]]
The work also revealed how European architectural styles had been adapted to local conditions.
Neoclassical elements, such as Doric and Ionic pilasters, dentil cornices, triangular pediments and egg-and-dart mouldings, were found to have been crafted with local lime plaster by Chinese craftsmen.
A distinctly Malayan interpretation of Art Deco was also uncovered.
"This can be seen in deeper window recesses to protect against tropical rain, greater roof overhangs, jalousie ventilation details and the use of Shanghai plaster - a weather-resistant aggregate finish - rather than smooth painted plaster.
"Decorative screens were also used in place of solid walls around stairwells, allowing air to circulate through the buildings," they said.
Other findings included chengal timber structures, a mixture of clay roof tiles for the square and remnants of original Madras terracotta clay floors.
"These discoveries show us that Medan Pasar is more than a collection of old facades.
"Its buildings contain evidence of the craftsmanship, climatic adaptation, cultural exchange and architectural evolution of early Kuala Lumpur."
But the restoration is not intended to turn Medan Pasar into a static heritage precinct.
The plan is to bring the area back to life with the arts, food and beverage, retail, businesses and community.
The Muara Arts Gallery, a not-for-profit public gallery celebrating Malaysian and Southeast Asian visual art, is scheduled to open on Nov 1, while the Muara Arts Theatre is planned for 2029.
The restoration of Seri Negara and Medan Pasar also forms part of the wider Warisan KL effort to revitalise Kuala Lumpur's historic core, bringing heritage spaces back into everyday use while preserving the stories embedded in their walls, floors and structures.

Title: N. Korea defence minister dismissed
Article:
SEOUL: North Korea's defence minister has been dismissed as part of a reshuffle of the country's military leadership, state media reported Sunday.
The "structural reorganisation plans" were decided during a meeting on Saturday led by Kim Jong Un, the Korean Central News Agency (KCNA) said.
No Kwang Chol was not only dismissed as defence minister but also demoted in the ruling party leadership to "first vice-director of the Munitions Industry Department", KCNA said.
Kim Song Gi, director of the General Political Bureau of the Korean People's Army, was named as the new defence minister.
Another senior official, defence adviser Pak Jong Chon, was given the position of vice-chairman of the Central Military Commission and named to the ruling party's Political Bureau.
Several other promotions were also announced.
In a separate report, KCNA said Kim had lauded scientists, researchers and officials at a ceremony on Saturday for their advances in defence technology, giving them top national honours.
The honourees greatly contributed to "resolving scientific and technological problems of epochal significance in developing new combat weapon systems", KCNA said, without specifying the type of system.
In late June, Kim oversaw tests of a new extended-range multiple rocket launcher and artillery.
The leadership shuffle comes shortly after joint annual drills between South Korea and the United States wrapped up.
The drills, which are regularly denounced by Pyongyang as preparations for an invasion, were closely watched this year after US President Donald Trump ordered them to be shortened.
Trump criticised the drills as provocative towards the North and bashed Seoul for not supporting his war against Iran.
The US president also praised North Korean leader Kim, whom he met twice during his first term in office, as he eyes a new meeting, potentially this year.
Despite Trump's overtures, North Korea has shown little sign of reciprocating, firing missiles and condemning the scaled-down drills.
Pyongyang has also slammed Washington's approval of arms sales to South Korea and plans to fund programmes documenting human rights abuses in the North.

Title: Inside the painstaking restoration of Bangunan Sultan Abdul Samad
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: To bring a 129-year-old landmark back to life, the team restoring Bangunan Sultan Abdul Samad (BSAS) first had to step back in time.
They had to think like its original builders, understand how it was designed, why certain materials were chosen and how the structure was put together more than a century ago.
Then the building began giving up its own secrets.
Old photographs helped the team recreate the original form of the clock tower dome, while restoration and hacking works uncovered features hidden for decades, including staircases buried beneath the building.
It was part construction, part detective work.
But restoring the building meant more than repairing what time had worn away. The team had to preserve its historic character while making room for modern needs.
The New Sunday Times spoke to contractors involved in restoring the Level 1 National Heritage site about the painstaking work that went into its return to public life.
The project covered BSAS, designated Block One, and the adjacent Old General Post Office, known as Block Two.
EVERY OLD BUILDING HAS ITS OWN STORY
For Kamal Engineering Sdn Bhd managing director Mustaffa Kamal Kamaluddin, heritage conservation begins with understanding the building before even touching it.
This means studying its history, materials, construction technology, alterations and significance before deciding what intervention is appropriate.
Moisture is among the biggest challenges faced by old buildings, particularly those constructed before modern damp-proofing methods became commonplace.
Rising damp from groundwater and moisture from leaking roofs can accelerate structural deterioration, leading to timber and roof rot, termite infestation and peeling paint.
[[nid:1521506]]
Mustaffa said BSAS had many timber components, including roof rafters, trusses and the internal structure of its domes.
These timber components need to be treated or replaced to ensure the building's longevity and durability.
During the project design stage, a dilapidation study and condition assessment of the building was carried out by a team consisting of conservators, architects and engineers.
"Preservation is the ultimate goal, repairing comes next. Replacing and reconstructing only comes into play when necessary," ?Mustaffa said.
He said in most cases where new materials were introduced, samples and mockups were prepared and tested for approval before final installation.
"To comply with laws and regulations, new spatial planning and materials may need to be introduced, which may affect the authenticity of the building."
Pengurusan Aset Warisan chief executive officer Hilme Hassan said striking a balance between preserving BSAS's historic character and adapting it for modern use was one of the biggest challenges to the restoration.
The building presented issues, including water seepage, mould and deteriorated structural elements and materials that had naturally weakened over time.
In some areas, previous repair work had concealed deeper problems.
"We could not simply address what was visible on the surface. We had to investigate carefully, understand the underlying condition and determine the most appropriate conservation treatment," Hilme said.
He said the clock tower's copper dome and two domes at the arcade towers were among the more technically demanding elements, having deteriorated beyond repair.
Hilme said the solution was not simply to replace old components with modern materials, but to understand the layers of history contained within the buildings.
"For us, that is ultimately what conservation is about. We're not trying to make an old building look brand new. We're trying to preserve its authenticity while preparing it for the next chapter of its life."
DOME WITHIN A DOME
[[nid:1521505]]
For BSAS, one of the most intricate parts of the restoration involved its clock tower and the three domes.
Kamal Engineering senior project manager Wan Mohd Sukri Wan Sulaiman said investigations into the existing dome showed that it had been altered from its original form over the years.
Historical photographs and old documents were used to establish what the 1897 structure originally looked like.
"The conservator wanted to revert it to the original 1897 design. Based on photographic references, we rebuilt it and produced a model that is almost exactly like the original."
However, reproducing the appearance did not mean reproducing every original construction method.
The original dome structure used timber, which had deteriorated over time. Rather than replacing it with new timber, the team redesigned the internal structure using aluminium while retaining copper on the exterior.
Wan Mohd Sukri said the modernised design incorporated a waterproofing membrane and an internal aluminium liner beneath the external copper.
The result is effectively a "dome within a dome".
"The outside still looks almost the same as the original, but the internal structure has been changed. We have engineers who specialise in redesigning it."
The team also had to find a way to work on the mini dome on the clock tower without damaging the historic structure beneath it.
Unlike conventional scaffolding, which can be tied directly to a building's walls, the scaffolding at BSAS could not be anchored into its original brickwork.
[[nid:1521504]]
Instead, a specially engineered tubular cantilever scaffold was installed from the lower levels towards the dome.
I-beams were inserted into the building to support the working platforms, allowing the scaffold to stand without being tied or screwed into the heritage walls.
The team also installed protection around the dome to shield it from prolonged exposure to rain and sunlight during the restoration.
WHEN GREEN ISN'T GOOD
The copper domes presented another challenge that may not be obvious from the ground: keeping them copper-coloured.
Untreated copper naturally oxidises when exposed to oxygen and moisture, eventually developing the green patina seen on older copper structures around the world, including on the Statue of Liberty.
That was not the appearance the restoration team wanted for BSAS.
Mustaffa said the copper had to be treated with a protective coating to slow oxidation and preserve the building's intended appearance.
The challenge is particularly relevant in Malaysia's hot and wet climate, as the copper will be exposed to rain and humidity.
New copper sheets, measuring about 0.7mm thick, were imported from Germany, while fabrication and installation involved local craftsmen.
Even the screws used for the cladding had to be considered carefully to minimise corrosion and maintain the appearance of the copper.
MASSIVE MAN HOURS
Beneath BSAS's distinctive arches and ornate facade is a building method that is increasingly unfamiliar to modern contractors: brick masonry without the reinforced concrete and steel commonly used today.
Wan Mohd Sukri said the building's brickwork required particular care because the original walls were not designed to accommodate modern construction methods.
The team also had to restore the mortar between the bricks, known as pointing.
The deteriorated material was removed and replaced with a specially formulated lime-based mixture rather than conventional cement.
This was because the historic brick walls were designed to "breathe", allowing moisture to move through the masonry, while cement could trap moisture and accelerate deterioration.
[[nid:1521503]]
Wan Mohd Sukri said some original bricks dating back to 1897 were identified through their markings.
But bricks that had become too brittle or deteriorated to remain in place could not simply be discarded.
"The damaged bricks were crushed and used as part of the process of producing replacement bricks, helping retain the characteristics of the original material."
The painstaking work required a workforce of more than 500 people, reaching about 600 workers at its peak as the BSAS project had to be completed in roughly a year.
That compressed timeline made coordination and quality control particularly demanding, with workers carrying out everything from cleaning and repointing brickwork to specialised restoration of architectural elements.
The facade also underwent treatment to prevent unwanted vegetation from taking root in the historic masonry.
Even the paint required a different approach. Instead of conventional acrylic paint, the team used lime-based paint for appropriate surfaces, allowing it to remain permeable.
OLD BUILDING, NEW SECRETS
During preparatory work for a new lift, the project team discovered an undocumented staircase hidden beneath the floor.
Careful excavation revealed five steps built from a mixture of sand and lime.
Rather than rebury the staircase, the team conserved it beneath a glass cover, allowing visitors to see the feature.
"It was a new finding. We did not know it was there because it had been covered," Wan Mohd Sukri said, adding that its discovery offered another glimpse into the building's earlier layout.
The first discovery proved to be only the beginning, with restoration works revealing another staircase hidden beneath a planter box outside the Old General Post Office.
Today, the staircase has been exposed and sits in full view in front of an eatery, offering another glimpse into the building's past.
[[nid:1521502]]
Hilme said another discovery is an original arch opening behind the reception counter which was concealed over time.
It had been restored, which enabled Masjid Jamek to be viewed directly from Dataran Merdeka through BSAS.
These discoveries are a reminder that with heritage buildings, the building itself is often one of your most important historical records.
"You can study drawings and photographs, but sometimes the most valuable evidence is literally hidden within the walls, underneath the floor or beneath layers of paint."
MODERN ENGINEERING MEETS OLD-WORLD CRAFTSMANSHIP
At BSAS, the conservation philosophy extended to the building's distinctive brickwork, arches, decorative ornaments, clock towers, copper domes and finials.
But recreating these details required more than modern machinery and materials.
The team needed craftsmen with specialised skills in traditional construction and copper work - skills that are increasingly difficult to find.
In some cases, craftsmen with the knowledge required for the restoration had already retired.
Mustaffa said the project team had to call some of them back from retirement to help with specialised conservation work.
Some heritage materials and specialised skills required to produce them are no longer available, especially locally."
Some timber components were also fabricated by craftsmen in Penang, while copper cladding work was carried out locally in Taiping and Seri Kembangan.
The team also reinstalled the finials that were believed to be taken down during World War 2. Restoring them, however, required another layer of specialised craftsmanship.
[[nid:1521501]]
Wan Mohd Sukri said the original copper finials were internally shaped using local hardwood timber, with the copper formed into receding onion-like shapes rising towards a sharp pinnacle.
Some specialised tooling for the finials had to be carried out abroad because the required machinery and expertise were not readily available locally.
The project, therefore, combined modern engineering with skills passed down through generations.
LABOUR OF LOVE
The specialised nature of the work also means heritage restoration is not simply another construction tender.
Contractors bidding for government conservation projects must meet the relevant Construction Industry Development Board registration and specialisation requirements.
For conservation work, this can include B03 Pemulihan dan Pemuliharaan, alongside other requirements depending on the project.
This is in addition to the specialist knowledge needed to understand traditional materials, historic construction methods and conservation principles.
Mustaffa reflected on his journey of heritage restoration.
He said while the finished product often takes the spotlight, the daily dedication required to restore these landmarks often goes unnoticed.
Sustaining our heritage, he said, is a collective journey through institutional support or public appreciation.
"Treating these historic structures as our shared cultural legacy ensures they continue to inspire for years to come," he said.
Mustaffa said a Heritage Maintenance Plan should be established once restoration is completed, with buildings placed under the care of experienced maintenance teams.
BSAS officially opened on April 4, 1897. It was reopened to the public on Feb 2 following extensive restoration supported by Dana Warisan under Warisan KL.

Title: No Dutch investigation into Mladic's death
Article:
THE HAGUE: A UN court said Saturday evening that Dutch authorities would not be conducting a criminal investigation into the death of Ratko Mladic, the convicted Bosnian Serb war criminal.
Mladic, who was serving life in prison in The Hague for genocide and war crimes committed during the 1992-1995 Bosnian war, died in hospital on Thursday after suffering several strokes in recent months.
His age has always been a matter of dispute. He claimed to have been born in March 1943, but the tribunal listed his birth year as 1942. Local media widely reported that he died at the age of 84.
The International Residual Mechanism for Criminal Tribunals said Dutch authorities had carried out the procedures required by national law.
[[nid:1521492]]
On Friday, they decided "that no criminal investigation would be opened and that they would not be conducting an autopsy", the statement added.
The Mechanism said it had also appointed a judge, Iain Bonomy, to conduct a separate investigation into Mladic's death. That inquiry was still ongoing and details, for the moment, were confidential, it added.
On Monday, days before Mladic's death, Serbian authorities had called for his release on health grounds for treatment in Serbia.
In May, the Mechanism had already rejected a request from his family for Mladic's release.
Mladic, who was arrested in Serbia in 2011, had the verdict against him confirmed on appeal in 2021.
One of the crimes ascribed to him was the July 1995 massacre of approximately 8,000 Bosnian men and boys in the eastern Srebrenica region – the worst such atrocity in Europe since WWII.
The Mechanism's role is to carry out the residual duties of the UN tribunals based in The Hague, including the International Criminal Tribunal for the former Yugoslavia, which convicted Mladic.

Title: Seven AUKU sections on student freedoms to get priority, says Zambry
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Seven sections of the Universities and University Colleges Act (AUKU) relating to students, including provisions on freedom, will be given priority in the process of repealing the Act, said Higher Education Minister Datuk Seri Dr Zambry Abdul Kadir.
He said seven of AUKU's 44 sections relate to students, while the rest cover matters including the establishment, administration and governance of universities.
Zambry said AUKU needed to be viewed in a broader context as it was not solely related to students, but served as the parent Act governing the establishment of universities.
"Matters related to AUKU have also been discussed at the Cabinet level and the details concerning it will continue to be refined.
"AUKU is the parent Act of universities, the main one for the establishment of a university. This means that without AUKU, there would be no university, except Universiti Malaya, which has an old Act, the 1961 Act. But all other universities do not have one, all of them depend on AUKU for their existence," he told reporters after the opening of the 2026 Higher Education Institutions Sports (SUKIPT) at the Universiti Malaya (UM) Arena here today.
Zambry said AUKU should be reviewed to reflect the country's development, including in education, in line with Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim's view that legal provisions relating to students should be reviewed.
He said follow-up measures would be taken to ensure the repeal process was carried out comprehensively.
Anwar had previously said the proposal to repeal AUKU was aimed, among other things, at giving students greater room to speak freely and develop their innovative capacity, creativity and critical thinking.

Title: 91 Malaysians remain uncontactable after Nepal, China floods
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A total of 91 Malaysians, comprising 55 in Nepal and 36 in China, remain uncontactable as of 8pm today following floods that struck on Aug 26, the Foreign Ministry said.
In a statement, the ministry said it would continue working closely with the relevant Chinese and Nepalese authorities while cross-checking figures from both countries to rule out duplicate reports.
It also urged the media and public to refer to figures issued by the ministry when reporting on Malaysians affected by the situation in Nepal and China, as the numbers could change when contact was established with those concerned and further reports were received from the relevant authorities and families.
"The ministry understands the heightened concern regarding the limited personal information released publicly on individual Malaysians who remain uncontactable," it said.
It added that, in accordance with established consular procedures, information on individual cases was provided directly to verified immediate next of kin.
Consular officers had contacted all verified immediate next of kin whose details were available to provide updates on the latest developments, it said.
The ministry said personal details would not be released publicly without the consent of the immediate next of kin.
"While the ministry appreciates the concern shown by friends, relatives and members of the wider public, the interests and welfare of the Malaysians currently reported as uncontactable, as well as those of their immediate families, remain the ministry's utmost priority.
"The ministry therefore urges all parties to respect the privacy of the affected families and to rely on official information as consular efforts continue," the statement read.
The ministry urged immediate next of kin who had yet to provide their details to contact its 24-hour operations room to assist Malaysians affected by the situation and their families.
They can be reached at +603 8887 4570 or dutyofficer@kln.gov.my.
Family members may also provide relevant details to the Embassy of Malaysia in Kathmandu at mwkathmandu@kln.gov.my or the Embassy of Malaysia in Beijing at mwbeijing@kln.gov.my, with a copy to the ministry's Operations Room.

Title: 23.4pct of KL children under 5 stunted, says Health Minister
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malnutrition among children under 5 in the Federal Territory of Kuala Lumpur is worrying, said Health Minister Datuk Seri Dr Dzulkefly Ahmad.
He said National Health and Morbidity Survey (NHMS) data showed that 23.4 per cent of children in Kuala Lumpur were stunted, while 12.4 per cent were underweight, 8.1 per cent affected by wasting and 7.5 per cent overweight.
"These figures are more than just statistics. Behind every percentage is a child going through a critical stage of development, and a family hoping for the support they need," he said when launching the Urban Community Feeding Programme (PCF Bandar) with Seputeh member of parliament Teresa Kok at the Muhibbah Community Complex here.
Dzulkefly said the country was grappling with a double burden of malnutrition, with undernutrition existing alongside overnutrition.
He said the Health Ministry was taking a proactive approach by going into communities to identify at-risk children who did not regularly attend health facilities.
As part of the intervention, he said the PCF Bandar model, introduced on a pilot basis in 2013, provides affected children aged 1 to 6 with 6 months of structured support, including monthly growth monitoring, nutritious food baskets, and fresh fruit and vegetables every two weeks.
In Seputeh, the 6-month intervention programme is being funded through a partnership with Kok, following similar programmes in the Lembah Pantai and Wangsa Maju constituencies.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Man died from injuries sustained in fall from height at Desa ParkCity, say police
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The post-mortem on the male suspect believed to have fallen from a condominium in Desa ParkCity, Kepong, on Thursday was completed this evening at the National Institute of Forensic Medicine, Hospital Kuala Lumpur.
City police chief Datuk Fadil Marsus said the findings revealed that the 48-year-old man's cause of death was multiple injuries consistent with a fall from a height.
"Both families are currently making arrangements to claim the remains for burial," he said in a brief statement tonight.
Earlier, the media reported that the man's wife and two children, who were found dead inside a unit at the same condominium, had died from stab wounds.
Fadil was reported as saying that post-mortems conducted yesterday on the seven-year-old boy and nine-year-old girl found their cause of death to be stab wounds to the neck.
Meanwhile, the
post-mortem
on the 47-year-old wife concluded that she died from sharp-force trauma to the neck and chest.
The tragedy, which claimed the lives of the four family members, is believed to have stemmed from the suspect's wife falling victim to a
love scam
.
The case is being investigated under Section 302 of the Penal Code for murder, as well as for sudden death.

Title: Queen graces UTM royal gala dinner 2026
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Her Majesty Raja Zarith Sofiah, Queen of Malaysia graced the Universiti Teknologi Malaysia (UTM) Royal Gala Dinner 2026 tonight.
UTM Pro-Chancellor Che Puan Mahkota Khaleeda Johor also graced the biennial event, which was also attended by UTM Pro-Chancellor Tan Sri Datuk Professor Emeritus Dr Mohd Zulkifli Mohd Ghazali and Japanese Ambassador to Malaysia Shikata Noriyuki.

The Royal Gala Dinner was also enlivened by entertainment and a special singing performance by guest artiste Wani Hasrita.

He said UTM received RM16 million in contributions this year from donors including Bidari Kekal Sdn. Bhd, Japan International Cooperation Agency (JICA), Johor Port Bhd, Awantec Systems Sdn Bhd and Permodalan Nasional Bhd.

Shafry said UTM's humanitarian spirit also transcended borders, with UTM having sponsored 10 Palestinian students to pursue Doctor of Philosophy studies at UTM since 2023 through the UTM Serambi Al-Quds Programme.

Title: Nepal flood death toll rises to 675
Article:
KATHMANDU: Devastating floods near the border with China this week have killed at least 675 people in Nepal, the Himalayan nation's disaster authority said on Saturday.
Chinese state media earlier confirmed seven dead in Tibet following Wednesday's disaster, taking the total killed to 682.
The number of missing in Nepal remained constant at 2,426, after a sharp hike in numbers on Saturday morning.
That missing list includes 517 foreigners, as well as 933 workers on hydropower projects on the river where the torrent smashed down, according to the National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority.
The number of missing also includes 45 Nepali Army soldiers, 40 police officers, and 19 immigration and customs officers.
In India, authorities said they had recovered seven bodies from rivers flowing from Nepal, believed to be flood victims. However, they are not included in the toll.
