Title: Men head to cosmetic clinics to complete weight-loss transformations
Article:
AS  top-selling weight-loss drugs help more men in the United States slim down, a growing number are seeking cosmetic treatments for sagging skin, hair loss and dental issues to complete their physical transformation, patients and plastic surgeons say.
Mark C, a 57-year-old from Hoboken, New Jersey, has spent the past five years taking obesity medications, first Novo Nordisk's Wegovy and then Eli Lilly's Zepbound, shedding 23kg in the process.
As the weight came off, so did some of the fullness in his face.
"I was looking at myself and I was feeling really good. I'm thinner and I feel like who I am, but I would look in the mirror and I was like, I lost volume in my face," the tech professional said.
In April, Mark opted for a deep-plane facelift, a procedure that repositions underlying facial muscles and fat.
Reuters spoke to six male patients and a dozen cosmetic surgeons who said weight-loss drugs, social media and changing perceptions of masculinity are sending more men to clinics that offer such procedures.
The trend reflects a broader shift in male attitudes towards cosmetic work, reshaping the clientele at aesthetic clinics and creating opportunities for companies developing treatments for the effects of rapid weight loss.
"I've seen probably a doubling in the number of male patients that I treat over the last one to two years," said Sean Alemi, Mark's doctor and a New York-based facial plastic surgeon.
He added that the majority of male patients came in after losing weight, most often as a result of GLP-1 therapies.
While women still account for the overwhelming majority of aesthetic treatments, demand among men has risen in recent years.
According to the American Society of Plastic Surgeons, men underwent 1.7 million cosmetic procedures in 2024, including surgeries and minimally invasive treatments such as laser skin resurfacing and Botox injections.
That was a 2.7 per cent increase from the previous year. Of the total, more than 98,000 were surgeries, with eyelid surgery, liposuction and tummy tucks among the most commonly performed.
In the first quarter of this year, nearly 70 per cent of men who underwent surgical procedures had a history of GLP-1 use, said Dr Bob Basu, president of the American Society of Plastic Surgeons.
Younger men often seek procedures to remove loose skin and improve the appearance of an athletic physique, while older men are focused on signs of ageing, particularly in the face and neck, doctors said.
Men accounted for 28.3 per cent of weight-loss drug prescriptions filled this year, up from 18.3 per cent four years earlier, according to GoodRx data.
"A man who may never previously have contemplated plastic surgery loses 50  or 80 pounds, starts lifting weights, changes his wardrobe, and becomes much more conscious of the disconnect between the healthier person he has become and the residual anatomy left behind by his former weight," said Miami-based plastic surgeon Dr Rian Maercks.
After reaching a weight-loss plateau with exercise alone, Walter Barrientos, 45, of Lancaster, California, joined a clinical trial for Eli Lilly's experimental drug retatrutide in November.
He has lost 29.4kg  overall and currently weighs 89.3kg.
"I want to be able to go out to the beach, to the pools, and be able to take off my shirt and feel more confident about myself," said Barrientos, a truck driver.
He had tummy tuck surgery, liposuction of the abdomen, flanks and chest, among other procedures, in July. Dental implants are next on his list.
Barrientos' Beverly Hills-based plastic surgeon, DrMichael Omidi, said his approach begins with understanding the specific concern that brings a patient in for a consultation.
"When a patient wants to have surgery, I think the rule is  if it  should bother you every day, then you can make that change," he said.
Mohammad Warrad, 27, had surgery with AirSculpt six months ago. The New York-based business owner felt his midsection was disproportionate to the rest of his body after using GLP-1 drugs.
"I had a skinny-fat body," Warrad said. "If the top part of my body was a medium (size of clothing), I had to wear an X-large just to kind of make everything look uniform," he said.
* The writer is from Reuters

Title: Gulf expats hunker down between bouts of  war
Article:
SIX  months into the Middle East war, the army of foreign workers and expatriates in the Gulf has largely stayed put —  hoping to ride out the uncertainty caused by conflict rather than return to dim prospects back home.
For most of the oil-rich Gulf states, foreigners from Global South countries make up the majority of the population, forming the bedrock of the economy as high-end consultants, manual labourers, healthcare professionals and everything in between.
Making it to the Gulf, where salaries are higher than at home, and untaxed, has long been a dream for those lucky enough to secure visas and employment.
But the war, which has killed 41 people in the Gulf, has proven to be incredibly disruptive for many.
In the United Arab Emirates, Dubai's service and tourism sectors have faced layoffs and salary cuts, and schools shifted to remote learning periodically, while in Kuwait many people skipped their summer holidays to avoid being trapped abroad due to air travel disruptions.
The ride has been bumpy, but most people have chosen to see it through, come what may.
"I stayed because I had no other option," a Syrian woman in her 30s, who asked to remain anonymous, said.
Even with the war and a salary cut, the options in Dubai are incomparable to those in Syria's shattered economy.
"Dubai is the place to be, to be secure, to hustle, to make money, to save — and that opportunity is not provided back home," she said. "Most of us are here because... it was just unliveable where we came from."
Like many people from the Global South working in the Gulf, her parents in Syria rely on her monthly remittances to make ends meet.
In the early weeks of the war, the UAE bore the brunt of Iran's wrath. Although the UAE shot down the large majority of the nearly 3,000 drones and missiles directed at the country, the war rattled its image as a haven of stability in a tumultuous Middle East.
More than 60,000 residents left Dubai as it came under heavy attack in March, but the population nonetheless grew to 4.73 million by July, topping pre-war numbers, according to official data.
In Bahrain's capital Manama, Indian waiter Rabin Sharma said he was out of the country at the onset of the war but raced towards the conflict, rather than away: he had to get back to his job.
Foreigners who have moved to the Gulf face a dilemma: leave their tax-free haven and face lower wages at home, or remain and hope for the best.
Some families have opted to move dependents back home while the breadwinner stays behind to continue earning money.
This was the case for an Egyptian engineer living in Kuwait — who also requested anonymity.
Sitting in a luxury cafe at a Kuwaiti mall, he said his wife and daughter would be returning to Egypt while he stayed put.
"I cannot risk their lives," he said. "The situation is too unstable."
Missiles and drones rained on the tiny Gulf nations of Kuwait and Bahrain in regular barrages throughout July as the US-Iran truce unravelled.
Kuwait reported repeated attacks on its only airport and on water desalination and power plants that forced authorities to ask residents to ration energy.
Amro Hussein, another Egyptian, said he fled the country by land with his wife and two young daughters after they awoke in the middle of the night to the sound of a drone crashing into a nearby building.
"It was a shock... especially for the children," he said.
But four months later, the family, which has lived in Kuwait for 12 years, decided to return together.
"It wasn't an easy decision," he said, "but honestly, my wife encouraged me — she's a brave person... She said no, let's stay put and keep the family together."
They decided they would stay even if more attacks targeted Kuwait.
Back in Dubai, Darly Lanzuela, 33, described going back to the Philippines as inconceivable, saying she makes "10 times" more working in a mall in the Gulf.
"To give my children a better future and secure their education, it's better to stay in Dubai."
* The writers are from AFP
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: NST Leader: Stop love scammers —  they are wanted for murder
Article:
THE horrific deaths of four members in a family at a condominium in Desa Parkcity, Kepong should force us to look at love scams as more than another category of online fraud.
To do this, we need to begin with a question: why do people continue to fall for increasingly sophisticated romance scams despite years of public warnings?
Romance scammers exploit something more powerful than greed: loneliness, trust, affection and the human desire for companionship. Once emotional dependence is established, victims can become remarkably resistant to warnings from family and friends.
Strong family and social ties can make people feel less isolated and ready to seek advice either from the family or social circles when they encounter strangers.
The issue also demands a rethink of how society talks about victims. Too often, those who lose money to love scams are dismissed as gullible or foolish.
Such stigma can drive victims further into isolation, make them reluctant to report the crime and allow scammers to continue manipulating them. This explains why only a small number of victims reported to the police.
Last year, 978 love scam cases were reported from January-November, with losses of RM43.7 million. In 2024,   770 cases were reported, mostly by women, with losses reaching 45.9 million.
In 2023, 935 victims, again mostly women, lodged reports. The police told Bernama in January 2025 after
Harian Metro
broke the story earlier that the most popular social media platforms were WhatsApp and Facebook.
Society must cease putting the blame on the victims and help victims and authorities fight romance scammers who are the ones to be truly to be blamed.
Paying greater attention to work-life balance will certainly help. Humans are social animals. We need to make time for family and friends, say psychologists, because staying connected means we can give support enabling us to talk openly when someone is struggling and step in when help is needed. Genuine human connection can help curb emotional exploitation by scammers.
There is also a wider question of responsibility. Banks, social media platforms, telecommunication companies, law enforcement agencies and families all have roles to play in identifying suspicious transactions and behaviour before losses become catastrophic.
But prevention cannot rely solely on technology. Greater awareness of the psychological tactics used by scammers is equally important.
The Desa ParkCity case is a grim reminder that the true cost of a scam cannot be measured simply by the amount appearing in a police report. Behind every figure are relationships, livelihoods, families and lives potentially destroyed.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Serian tops hazardous API chart at 364, multiple Sarawak districts suffer worsening air
Article:
KUCHING, Aug 30 — Serian recorded a hazardous Air Pollutant Index (API) reading as of 8am today.
According to the Department of Environment (DOE)’s Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS) portal, the API reading at the Serian District Police Headquarters monitoring station stood at 364.
Meanwhile, three areas in Sarawak recorded very unhealthy API readings, namely Samarahan (300), Kuching (291) and Sri Aman (214).
Areas recording unhealthy API readings include Sarikei (195), Sibu (187), Bintulu (179), Samalaju (171), Mukah (170), Kapit (159), Miri (155) and the Miri Industrial Training Institute (ILP) (151).

API figures are updated hourly based on readings from 68 monitoring stations nationwide. — Bernama

Title: Early morning fire in Kota Kinabalu squatter area, 39 personnel deployed to contain blaze
Article:
KOTA KINABALU, Aug 30 — A fire broke out at stilt houses in a squatter area in Kampung Numbak here early this morning, with the number of houses involved yet to be confirmed as firefighters continue to battle the blaze.
The Sabah Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM), in a statement, said it received an emergency call at 1.40am, following which firefighters were deployed and arrived at the scene, located 18 kilometres away, at 1.58am.
“A total of 39 personnel from the Kota Kinabalu, Lintas and Penampang Fire and Rescue Stations (BBP) were deployed to the scene to carry out firefighting operations,” it said.
According to the Sabah JBPM, firefighters were battling the blaze using two streams and four water jets, with water supplied by fire engines.
Efforts to extinguish the fire are still ongoing, and further information on the incident will be provided from time to time.
No information on victims has been received so far, with the Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM) and other relevant agencies also assisting in the firefighting operations. — Bernama

Title: Beyond monuments and textbooks, KL’s Statesman Memorial guards Malaysia’s nation‑building story
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 30 — As Malaysia turns 69, the country has witnessed its fair share of history — from the struggle for independence and the formation of the federation to almost seven decades of nation-building, political change and rapid development.
Yet much of that history lives on not only in records and textbooks, but also in the places where key decisions were made and in the stories of those who helped shape the country through its formative years.
One such place is the Statesman Memorial (also known as Memorial Negarawan), housed in the former Prime Minister’s Office (PMO) along Jalan Dato Onn, which bears witness to the country’s post-independence administrative history.
Built in 1957 along what was then known as Brockman Road, the Brutalist-inspired building was built to replace Tunku Abdul Rahman’s
Old Office Building
nearby, and later served for decades as the seat of the federal government and the workplace of Malaysia’s prime ministers.
National Archives of Malaysia (ANM) director-general Zaidin Mohd Noor said the building’s historical significance lies not merely in its role as an administrative office, but as a physical witness to Malaysia’s journey in governance and development.
“One lesser-known aspect of the building is that it was more than just the PMO; it was also an important setting for government deliberations and decision-making in post-independence Malaysia.
“During its years of operation, various government policies, development plans, security issues, international relations and decisions that significantly impacted the lives of Malaysians were discussed and implemented there,” he told
Malay Mail
during a recent interview.
ANM director-general Zaidin Mohd Noor speaks to Malay Mail during an interview. — Picture by Yusof Isa
The former Prime Minister’s Office housed the tenures of Tun Abdul Razak Hussein, Tun Hussein Onn and Tun Dr Mahathir Mohamad — who occupied the office for the longest period, 22 years — until the federal government administrative centre moved to Putrajaya in 2003.
While museums and historical galleries typically bring collections and artefacts into exhibition spaces, Zaidin said the Statesman Memorial instead takes visitors to an actual site directly connected to the country’s administrative history, offering them a distinctly different experience.
Beyond its administrative role, Zaidin said the building itself was also a setting for significant moments in Malaysia’s diplomatic history, hosting notable foreign figures in 1990, including Nelson Mandela, then deputy president of the African National Congress, and Yasser Arafat, chairman of the Palestine Liberation Organisation.
“What makes the Statesman Memorial particularly distinctive is the building’s authenticity.
“Rather than being purpose-built as a new exhibition space, the memorial occupies a historic building that once served as a centre of government administration,” he said.
Where history lives
Beyond displaying documents, photographs, collections and materials related to the nation’s statesmen, the Statesman Memorial also retains elements and spaces linked to the building’s original function.
Key preserved spaces include the former Prime Minister’s Office and the Cabinet meeting room, which remain largely intact with their original setup.
The meeting room where Cabinet meetings were held every Wednesday, with Dr Mahathir presiding over the final meeting there on June 16, 1999. — Picture by Yusof Isa
Another notable exhibit is the original setup of the Baling Talks, held at Baling English School as depicted in history books, where negotiations between the Malayan government and communist representatives attempted to resolve the Malayan Emergency after World War II.
This in turn allows visitors not only to see history, but also in some instances, to experience the very spaces where it unfolded.
For younger generations, experiencing these spaces first-hand could deepen their appreciation of Malaysia’s development and foster a stronger sense of history, identity and civic responsibility, Zaidin added.
“In heritage preservation, authenticity is one of the most important values. As such, preserving spaces such as the PMO and Cabinet meeting room carries significance beyond simply retaining a room or its furniture layout.
“The arrangement of tables, chairs, documents, equipment and other elements within the room can help visitors envision how the country’s leaders carried out their duties, deliberated and made decisions while fulfilling their responsibilities.
“The spaces also symbolise the continuity of Malaysia’s governing institutions, preserving not just the physical rooms but the memories and meaning embedded within them,” he said.
The old Prime Minister’s Office was first occupied by Abdul Razak on Sept 22, 1970, and remained in use until Dr Mahathir vacated it on Oct 31, 2003. — Picture by Yusof Isa
More importantly, Zaidin said a country’s history is not always shaped by major events witnessed by the public, but also through the deliberations and decisions made behind closed doors.
“Ultimately, the building stands as a physical witness to nation-building, where national leaders made decisions that shaped Malaysia’s policies and direction.
“Therefore, its historical value lies not only in who occupied it, but also in the many affairs of state that took place within its walls,” he said.
Following the federal government’s move to Putrajaya, the former PMO received a facelift nearly a decade later in 2012 and was developed into what it is today after the Cabinet approved the memorial’s establishment at the site with RM30 million in funding under the 10th Malaysia Plan.
Seven figures, shared legacy
In actuality, the memorial chronicles the contributions of seven statesmen from Peninsular Malaysia, Sabah and Sarawak — Tun Dr Ismail Abdul Rahman, Tun Tan Cheng Lock, Tun VT Sambanthan, Tun Dr Lim Chong Eu, Tun Datu Mustapha Datu Harun, Tun Fuad Stephens and Tun Jugah Barieng.
“The seven were chosen for their significant contributions to the country, including their roles in the struggle for independence, shaping key national policies, community development and strengthening national unity.
“The inclusion of figures from Sabah and Sarawak also recognises their roles in the formation of Malaysia in 1963, reflecting the country’s history as a federation built on cooperation across regions and communities,” Zaidin said.
An office setup of former deputy prime minister Tun Dr Ismail Abdul Rahman, including personal items at the Statesman Memorial. — Picture by Yusof Isa
In each statesman’s gallery, exhibits include correspondence, photographs, personal collections and official records, offering visitors a glimpse into their thoughts, principles and leadership values.
While the statesmen are often remembered for their nation-building roles, Zaidin said there are many lesser-known stories and fascinating facts featured at the memorial that may be unfamiliar to the public.
“For example, Tan’s collection includes documents from around 1946 and 1954 that offer insights into political debates of the time, including the Malayan Union, democracy, elections and voting rights, helping visitors understand the challenges and ideas that shaped the country before independence.
“What makes the stories of the seven statesmen particularly compelling is their diverse backgrounds, yet their contributions complemented one another in building the nation.
“Their stories show that Malaysia’s development was not the work of a single leader or community, but the result of the struggles, cooperation, courage and commitment of many,” he said.
Personal items on display at former MIC president Tun VT Sambanthan’s gallery at the Statesman Memorial. — Picture by Yusof Isa
Although preserving the entire building is part of ANM’s responsibility to safeguard the country’s physical heritage and administrative memory, Zaidin said the Statesman Memorial ultimately goes beyond being a place to learn about the seven statesmen.
“It brings together the figures, documents, building and historic spaces to offer an authentic experience of Malaysia’s past, giving the memorial distinctive historical and educational value, particularly for younger generations,” he said.

Title: As cyber threats strike at AI speed, Malaysia urged to embed risk‑based defence
Article:
CYBERJAYA, Aug 29 — In the nearly 30 years since Malaysia began developing its national cyber emergency response capabilities with the establishment of MyCERT, the most significant change has been not merely the growing volume of cyber threats, but the speed at which attacks can occur, now further accelerated by artificial intelligence (AI).
Telekom Malaysia Chief Information Security Officer Raja Azrina Raja Othman, who was among the co-founders of MyCERT in 1997, said cyber threats three decades ago were largely confined to specific systems and networks.
Today, however, almost all services operate digitally and are interconnected, ranging from banking and government services to corporate operations and national critical infrastructure.
“When a cyberattack occurs, the impact goes beyond mere system downtime. It can compromise operations, finances, customer data and reputation, as well as disrupt services relied upon by the public,” she said in a special interview held in conjunction with the recent launch of TM’s 80th-anniversary celebrations, officiated by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim.
She added that another major shift was the sheer speed at which cyberattacks could now be launched, with AI further accelerating the process.
“With AI, cyber attackers can more easily identify vulnerabilities, craft more convincing phishing campaigns and launch attacks at a much faster pace.
“Cyber attackers today operate rapidly with the aid of AI. Therefore, cyber defence strategies can no longer rely solely on manual processes,” she said.
Raja Azrina said the real challenge lies in increasingly complex information infrastructures driven by extensive application integration.
A lack of alignment between IT planning and information security could increase an organisation’s exposure to cyber threats, she said.
However, she observed that some organisations still viewed cybersecurity as an optional measure rather than an essential component of their operations.
“In reality, cybersecurity is a matter of risk management and business continuity. If core systems are compromised, can the organisation continue to operate? Can we maintain service delivery to customers? And will they retain confidence in our business?
“These are the questions organisations must address,” she added.
Therefore, she said, responsibility for cybersecurity must start with leadership and be embedded within organisational governance.
She stressed that cybersecurity investments should be guided by a risk-based approach, with organisations prioritising risks according to their potential impact on business operations.
“Even with cybersecurity investments, we cannot assume that attacks can be prevented entirely. Instead, we must be prepared for the possibility that an incident could still occur.
“What distinguishes truly prepared organisations is their ability to detect threats early, respond swiftly and remediate issues without causing prolonged disruption to operations.
“In cybersecurity, we cannot wait until a crisis strikes before deciding who needs to take action,” she said.
Raja Azrina said cybersecurity was not a new field for TM, as it had long been part of the company’s responsibility to manage and protect the nation’s digital infrastructure.
“TM’s cybersecurity capabilities are built on years of experience in protecting our own operations and supporting the digital needs of enterprises and the government, covering networks, cloud services, data centres and applications,” she said.
“Our teams continuously monitor security, drawing on their experience in managing vast and complex digital environments,” she added.
She noted that TM also had local cybersecurity experts specialising in various areas, including threat detection and monitoring, incident response and digital forensics.
“Based on our experience, cybersecurity monitoring and controls are required at every level - network, infrastructure and application - to establish layered protection and enhance the effectiveness of detection and response,” she said.
For Raja Azrina, the question today is no longer whether organisations will adopt AI, but whether they can do so securely while maintaining the trust of customers and the public, as security measures must evolve as rapidly as technology.
She said this was one of the key reasons TM developed the TM Cyber Defence Centre (TM CYDEC).
Through a “Cyber Fusion” approach, TM CYDEC enables comprehensive monitoring of cybersecurity issues across network, infrastructure and application security for the industry and government sectors. TM also has an AI security framework in place to govern AI security.
“We believe that the right cybersecurity strategy, a risk-based approach, and effective services and technologies can help organisations detect and respond to cyber threats earlier, thereby minimising their impact on business.
“Ultimately, our goal is to enable organisations to continue innovating and leveraging AI with confidence, without compromising security and trust,” she said. — Bernama

Title: Immigration to seek Thai details on syndicate trafficking China nationals from Cambodia into Malaysia
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 29 — The Immigration Department will work with Thai authorities to obtain detailed information on an alleged syndicate trafficking China nationals from Cambodia to Malaysia.
Immigration director-general Datuk Zakaria Shaaban said they were monitoring developments of the case even though they have yet to receive any official report on such activities.
“We will get further information from Thai authorities on this matter,” he said when contacted by Bernama today, after Thai media outlets reported that Thai authorities arrested two individuals suspected of being masterminds of a ring trafficking China nationals from the Cambodian border to Malaysia through Thailand.
Thai authorities found six China nationals and a Myanmar national who were waiting to be smuggled into Malaysia to work in a scam syndicate during a raid on a resort in Na Mom district in Songkhla province.
Thai authorities also identified four Thai nationals believed to be involved in the ring, including the individual arranging the immigrants’ journey from the Cambodia-Thai border to Hat Yai and onwards through to Malaysia. — Bernama

Title: Anwar: ‘Not a zero‑sum game’ as language mastery broadens unity and opportunity
Article:
PERMATANG PAUH, Aug 29 — Efforts to uphold Malay, the country’s official language, should not be seen as an attempt to undermine proficiency in other languages, said Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim.
He said every citizen, regardless of racial background, should have a good command of the national language, while at the same time, proficiency in other languages such as English, Mandarin and Tamil should continue to be strengthened to broaden educational and economic opportunities.
“We also know that English is a language that has developed into an important global language, so our system should embrace it, not replace Malay but complement it,” he said in his speech at the Ambang Merdeka Sahabat Madani 2026 highlight programme at Universiti Teknologi MARA (UiTM) Permatang Pauh here today.
Elaborating, Anwar said proficiency in Mandarin was becoming increasingly important given its position as one of the region’s major economic languages, while Malaysians were also interested in improving their proficiency in Tamil.
“It is not a zero-sum game. I encourage children to master the Chinese language, provided that their command of Malay is sufficiently good. Learning the languages of the region does not put us at a disadvantage.
“It’s an economic imperative to secure your own interest and your future. It is not done at the expense of English or American English. It is done to give you further opportunity to enhance and develop your potential,” he said.
The Prime Minister also reminded the people not to sow seeds of hostility among the races, as the country’s harmony cannot be taken for granted as something that will last forever without consistent efforts to preserve unity.
He stressed that a spirit of sharing, caring and helping one another must be instilled so that every citizen, regardless of race, can enjoy the benefits of the country’s development in an inclusive manner. — Bernama

Title: Anwar extends Malaysia’s condolences to Norway on passing of King Harald V
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 29 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today extended condolences on behalf of the Malaysian government to the people of Norway on the passing of King Harald V.
Anwar said King Harald would be remembered for his generous understanding of what it meant to be Norwegian, including his recognition of the country’s diverse society.
“He spoke of a country made up of people whose families came from Afghanistan, Pakistan, Poland and many other places, and affirmed that they, too, were Norwegian.
“His words were a reminder that a nation draws strength from the dignity it accords all its people,” he said in a statement via his Facebook,today.
Anwar said King Harald also understood the weight of an oath and the importance of remaining true to one’s commitments.
“Malaysia joins the people of Norway in mourning his passing,” the Prime Minister said.
King Harald V died on Friday at age 89 at the National Hospital in Oslo, after having been hospitalised since Aug 17 and was receiving cortisone treatment for hemolytic anemia. — Bernama

Title: Subang Jaya police open investigation into viral Facebook claim against officers
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 29 — Police have opened an investigation paper regarding a Facebook post that allegedly contained defamatory statements against police officers at a petrol station in Batu 14, Puchong, Selangor yesterday.
Subang Jaya district police chief ACP Wan Azlan Wan Mamat said his department received a report from a police officer who was on duty at the time of the incident at 10.54pm.
“The police have opened an investigation paper following the allegations under Section 500 of the Penal Code and Section 233 of the Communications and Multimedia Act 1998.
“The owner of the account will be traced immediately to assist in the investigation,” he said in a statement today.
He said the post uploaded by the owner of the Facebook account using the name ‘Izz Fairuzz’ was traced after it went viral on social media.
According to Wan Azlan, the post claimed that a police patrol vehicle blocked traffic while the personnel involved were allegedly waiting for food from a foreign trader at the petrol station without paying.
In this regard, he advised the public not to make any speculation regarding the allegations that went viral on social media.
“The public is requested to give the police full space to conduct further investigations without making any speculation,” he said.
He also asked individuals with information related to the incident to contact the Subang Jaya IPD district control centre at 03-7862 7100.
He said the identity of the informant would be kept confidential. — Bernama

Title: MAHA Expo hall closed after smoke incident, visitors evacuated as safety checks carried out
Article:
SERDANG, Aug 29 — Exhibition Hall A (Hall A) at the Malaysia Agro Exposition Park Serdang (MAEPS) was temporarily closed today following a minor incident involving smoke and an unpleasant odour at 4.50pm.
According to a statement posted on the official Expo MAHA 2026 Facebook page, the Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM) was called to the scene to carry out further checks as a precautionary measure.
“To ensure the safety and comfort of everyone, members of the public and exhibitors in Hall A are advised to calmly evacuate the hall with immediate effect until further notice,” it said.
It said Hall A would only be reopened after the authorities had confirmed that it was safe, adding that the safety of visitors, exhibitors and personnel remained the organisers’ top priority.
“We take this matter seriously and greatly appreciate your cooperation and patience. Further updates will be provided from time to time,” it said.
The Malaysia Agriculture, Horticulture and Agrotourism Show (MAHA) is being held at MAEPS from Aug 28 to Sept 6, bringing together about 2,000 exhibitors and targeting more than four million visitors. — Bernama

Title: Anwar: Colonial‑era laws curbing student freedom must be abolished to realise true independence
Article:
PERMATANG PAUH, Aug 29 — Colonial-era laws restricting students’ freedom should be abolished to allow the true meaning of independence to be fully realised, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said.
He said university students should have more freedom to voice their views and take part in activities, as they would play a key role in shaping the country’s future.
“That is why I announced last week that we would abolish university laws that restrict student activities. Older people are not always right either, so we should not prevent young people from speaking out or taking part in activities just because they make mistakes. They need to be given space.
“Freedom does not mean there should be no limits. This is a country governed by the rule of law. But I do not agree with adding laws to restrict or intimidate university students. This is an independent country, and laws inherited from the colonial past must be abolished,” he said.
He was speaking at the 2026 Sahabat MADANI Merdeka Eve programme at Universiti Teknologi MARA (UiTM) Penang Branch in Permatang Pauh today.
He said young people should be trusted to put forward their views and ideas, with mistakes addressed through the appropriate channels where necessary.
The Prime Minister said the approach would help develop a younger generation that could express themselves confidently, act responsibly and contribute to Malaysia’s development as an independent nation.
Anwar said independence meant more than freedom from physical colonisation, it also meant giving people the space to determine the country’s own future.
He said young people should learn from the history of the struggle for independence and build on it by helping Malaysia achieve greater progress and earn greater respect internationally. — Bernama

Title: GRS to lead seat talks, Hajiji says coalition preparing machinery ahead of GE16
Article:
KOTA KINABALU, Aug 29 — Gabungan Rakyat Sabah (GRS), as the coalition leading the Sabah government, will take the lead in determining seat allocations with its government allies for the next general election, said Chief Minister Datuk Seri Hajiji Noor.
Hajiji, who is also Parti Gagasan Rakyat Sabah (PGRS) president, said the coalition would eventually discuss the distribution of parliamentary seats with parties currently in the state government, including Pakatan Harapan (PH) and Barisan Nasional (BN).
“GRS is the main coalition leading the state government, so we will discuss with our partners the distribution of seats to be contested,” he told reporters after chairing a PGRS political meeting here today.
He said, however, that formal negotiations had yet to begin.
Hajiji said the main consideration would be to field candidates capable of winning the election.
“We hope our friends in the government will be rational and we will field those who can win in the election,” he said.
The GRS coalition consists of six parties — PGRS, Parti Bersatu Sabah (PBS), Parti Solidariti Tanah Airku (STAR), Liberal Democratic Party (LDP), Parti Harapan Rakyat Sabah (PHRS), Parti Cinta Sabah (PCS) and most recently, United Progressive Kinabalu Organisation (UPKO).
Hajiji said the party needed to start preparing for the general election now by strengthening its machinery at all levels and increasing its engagement with voters.
The remarks came as PGRS began restructuring its grassroots machinery along parliamentary constituencies, with the party today announcing 25 division chiefs following approval from the Registrar of Societies (ROS).
“As a party leading the government, we must be prepared from now and mobilise the party at all levels, including the wings, by going down to the grassroots and holding programmes,” he said.
He said the party would continue working on the ground despite the current parliamentary term only being expected to expire at the end of next year.
Among the 25 division chiefs appointed are Hajiji for Tuaran, state Finance Minister Datuk Seri Masidi Manjun for Ranau, state Agriculture, Fisheries and Food Industry Minister Datuk Dr Mohd Arifin Mohd Arif for Kimanis and state Local Government and Housing Minister Datuk James Ratib for Beluran.
Four of the appointments are new to the division chief line-up — Kota Marudu, Putatan, Semporna and Kalabakan.
PGRS said the restructuring was intended to strengthen its organisation at parliamentary and grassroots levels, expand membership and improve its ability to engage with voters.
Hajiji said those not appointed as division chiefs would still be given roles within the party, including as deputy or vice-heads and coordinators at state constituency level.
On Parti Kesejahteraan Demokratik Masyarakat (KDM), Hajiji said the party was not part of GRS, although its elected representative for Paginatan had expressed support for the state government.
He said cooperation with parties currently in the state administration would continue, while discussions on the distribution of seats would be held with its partners when the time came.
The restructuring of PGRS divisions will now proceed with the appointment of party members and committees before their membership lists are submitted to ROS.

Title: Traffic crawls along 20km stretch entering Kelantan as school break and National Day surge builds
Article:
GUA MUSANG, Aug 29 — Traffic entering Kelantan has been reported to be moving slowly along a stretch of about 20 kilometres at the border entry point between Merapoh, Pahang, and Kampung Mentara, Gua Musang, due to an increase in vehicles in conjunction with the school holidays and National Day celebration this Monday.
Gua Musang district police chief Supt Sik Choon Foo said traffic police personnel and the Mobile Patrol Vehicle (MPV) unit have been deployed to the location to conduct regular patrols.
“Police are closely monitoring traffic flow along all major routes to ensure the safety and smooth movement of road users.
“Congestion was detected at the diversion area of the Central Spine Road construction project, causing traffic to slow down from Merapoh to the end of the highway at Kampung Mentara,” he told Bernama today.
However, he said traffic flow returned to normal after passing the diversion area.
“So far, the number of vehicles on the road is indeed high, but traffic in Gua Musang town remains smooth without any unusual congestion,” he said.
Meanwhile, a Bernama check around 5pm today in Gua Musang town heading towards Kuala Krai found traffic to be smooth despite an increase in the number of vehicles since this morning.
In an earlier statement, PLUS Malaysia Berhad (PLUS) said traffic on its highways is expected to reach 2.2 million vehicles on peak days between Aug 28 and 31 and Sept 4 and 7 in conjunction with the National Day celebration and school holidays.
PLUS also advised road users to plan their journeys by referring to the MyPLUS-TTA digital travel schedule via the PLUS App to help distribute traffic flow and reduce vehicle concentration during peak periods. — Bernama

Title: ‘We can only pray’: Family of missing Malaysian in Nepal tragedy anxiously awaits news
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 29 — “Only prayer and patience can strengthen our spirits,” lamented Mures, the eldest son of senior citizen K. Balasingam, 71, who has yet to be contacted following the flash flood disaster on the Nepal-Tibet border on Wednesday.
Mures, 40, said his father’s journey to perform a religious ceremony on Mount Kailash, Tibet turned into a terrifying nightmare for the family after he was last seen active on the WhatsApp application on the morning of the incident.
“My father alone joined a group with 16 other Malaysians to Mount Kailash in Tibet, China to perform a religious ceremony.
“He arrived there on August 23 and was supposed to return to Malaysia on September 6 but until now our family has not received any information about him after the incident,” he said when contacted by Bernama today.
Describing his father’s personality, Mures described the former businessman in the transport sector who hails from Negeri Sembilan as someone who is very active in leisure and religious activities despite his age.
He said the family had contacted various parties to obtain the latest information including the Malaysian Embassy in Kathmandu and the police.
“So far we are still patient and do not know how long we will have to wait for developments regarding my father.
“We also received information from a member of the group who is in Nepal but until now there is no latest news. We continue to pray that my father is safe,” he said.
Balasingam was among 17 Malaysians in a group managed by Nepal-based travel agency Fishtail Tours & Travels.
The Foreign Ministry today said 55 Malaysians were still unreachable following the devastating flash floods and landslides in Rasuwa District, Nepal, on Wednesday. — Bernama

Title: Air quality worsens, two Sarawak stations breach very unhealthy levels, 29 areas nationwide unhealthy
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 29 — Two monitoring stations in Sarawak recorded very unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings as of 4pm today, while 29 other areas nationwide registered unhealthy air quality.
According to data from the Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS) portal, the API readings at Sri Aman and the Serian district police headquarters (IPD) monitoring station reached 229 and 228, respectively.
Areas recording unhealthy API levels included Sarikei in Sarawak (194), Sungai Petani in Kedah (161), Cheras in Kuala Lumpur (160), Minden in Penang (158), Taiping in Perak (158), Shah Alam in Selangor (157), Putrajaya (155), Seremban in Negeri Sembilan (151), and Segamat in Johor (132).
Meanwhile, 36 areas recorded moderate air quality, including Pegoh Ipoh in Perak (99), Banting in Selangor (95), Bukit Rambai in Melaka (92), Tangkak in Johor (90), Besut in Terengganu (88), Kota Bharu in Kelantan (87), and Kota Kinabalu in Sabah (86).
An API reading of zero to 50 indicates good air quality, 51 to 100 (moderate), 101 to 200 (unhealthy), 201 to 300 (very unhealthy), and above 300 (hazardous).
API figures are updated hourly based on readings from 68 monitoring stations nationwide. — Bernama

Title: MetMalaysia warns of thunderstorms and heavy rain in six states and KL until 7pm
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 29 — The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) has warned of thunderstorms, heavy rain and strong winds in seven states and Kuala Lumpur until 7pm today.
MetMalaysia said the warning was issued for the entire state of Kelantan and 11 districts in Perak: Batang Padang, Muallim, Hulu Perak, Kuala Kangsar, Kinta, Kampar, Perak Tengah, Larut Matang, Selama, Hilir Perak and Bagan Datuk.
The warning also covers Hulu Terengganu, Dungun, Besut, Setiu, Kuala Nerus, Kuala Terengganu and Marang in Terengganu, and Lipis, Cameron Highlands, Rompin, Raub, Bentong, Jerantut and Temerloh in Pahang.
The two other states affected are Selangor, covering Sabak Bernam, Kuala Selangor, Hulu Selangor, Gombak and Petaling, and Johor, covering Kluang, Mersing, Kota Tinggi and Segamat. — Bernama

Title: Anwar says Malaysia’s success must be anchored by a knowledgeable, disciplined generation
Article:
BATU KAWAN, Aug 29 — A country’s success should not be measured solely by economic and technological progress, but must also be supported by the development of a knowledgeable and disciplined younger generation, said Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim.
The Prime Minister said young people should be provided with an education that also instils values, a spirit of service and a sense of responsibility towards their families, society and country.
“What is the meaning of development, what is the meaning of a country’s success if our children are not instilled with spirit, education, discipline and love? That is why our children must have such a spirit.
“Why do we acquire knowledge at schools, institutions of higher learning and universities? It is to become knowledgeable and morally upright individuals who are able to serve society, their parents and also the country. This is a culture that must be nurtured,” he said.
Anwar said this when officiating the 15th Malaysian Scouts Jamboree (MYJAM15) at the Penang State Stadium here today. Also present were Chief Minister Chow Kon Yeow and Chief Scout Datuk Prof Dr Mohd Zin Bidin.
Commenting on current challenges, Anwar said that in navigating the rapid advancement of information technology and artificial intelligence (AI), the younger generation must not neglect their cultural roots and values, which form the foundation of society.
He said technological changes must be accompanied by the ability of the younger generation to adapt to new challenges without sacrificing the values and heritage that shape their identity.
The Prime Minister also stressed the importance of fostering unity in diversity, given that the younger generation would be the country’s future leaders.
Ahead of the 2026 National Day celebrations, he also urged the younger generation to continue nurturing their spirit of patriotism and be prepared to face future tests and challenges.
MYJAM15, which runs from today until Sept 4, brings together more than 5,450 local and international scouts from 11 countries, including South Korea, Indonesia, Singapore and Sri Lanka.
This year’s jamboree also marks a milestone as the national event returns to Penang after 60 years, since the state first hosted the event in Teluk Bahang in 1966. — Bernama

Title: Desa ParkCity family tragedy takes new turn as police reveal illegal investment issue alongside alleged love scam
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 29 — Police investigating the deaths of a family of four at a Desa ParkCity condominium in Kepong have revealed that the couple had also become entangled in an illegal investment scheme, adding a new dimension to a case already linked to an alleged love scam and RM260,000 in losses and debt.
Kuala Lumpur police chief Datuk Fadil Marsus said relatives of the couple were aware of both issues.
“The family knew about the love scam problem and that they had become trapped in an illegal investment scheme.
“The allegations involving the love scam, the existence of a scammer, as well as the RM260,000 in losses and debts, are still under investigation,” he said in a statement today.
The latest disclosure broadens the financial circumstances police are examining following the deaths at the condominium in Desa ParkCity on Wednesday.
Yesterday, investigators said they were looking into whether pressure over the RM260,000 debt, after his wife allegedly fell victim to a love scam, could have driven the 48-year-old man to kill his wife, 47, and their two children, aged nine and seven, before taking his own life.
The speculation followed the discovery of a note believed to have been left by the father on the dining table of the family’s Desa ParkCity home.

Title: Wisma Putra: 55 Malaysians still uncontactable as checks expand to Nepal–China border areas
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 29 — Fifty-five Malaysians remain uncontactable following the floods and landslides that struck Rasuwa District, Nepal on August 26, according to Malaysia’s Foreign Ministry.
“Two Malaysians previously reported as uncontactable have since been contacted, and verification of the remaining cases is ongoing,” the ministry, widely known as Wisma Putra, said in its latest statement updating the situation in Nepal and surrounding areas.
The Embassy of Malaysia in Kathmandu continues to work with the Emergency Response Team of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Nepal, the Nepal Tourism Board, travel agencies and relevant local authorities.
“Search and rescue operations in Nepal remain ongoing, while authorities are also monitoring the risk of further water surges from the Tibet Autonomous Region, China,” it said.
As at 5.00 pm Nepal time (7.15 pm Malaysia time) August 28, 2026, the National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority of Nepal reported that 771 people had been rescued, including 116 foreign nationals.
“Based on the official list available at this stage, no Malaysian has been identified among the foreign nationals rescued to date,” said Wisma Putra.
Wisma Putra said it has expanded its consular response to include Malaysians stranded in China due to travel disruptions arising from the floods and landslides in Nepal.
“A group of 72 Malaysians in Darchen, China, has been confirmed safe and in good health,” it said.
Wisma Putra said the Embassy of Malaysia in Beijing is in contact with the group, and their families are aware of their status.
“The Embassy is providing consular assistance, including support for their travel arrangements to leave the Tibet Autonomous Region, China,” it said.
Separately, the ministry said it had received information from the Chinese authorities and family members regarding 36 Malaysians who are currently reported as uncontactable in areas affected by telecommunications disruptions.
“The ministry is working closely with the Chinese authorities and family members to establish contact with the individuals concerned.
“The information is also being cross-checked against reports involving Malaysians in Nepal to identify any duplication as verification continues,” it said.
The Ministry’s Operations Room in Putrajaya has been operating around the clock since August 27, 2026, to coordinate information and assist Malaysians in the affected areas and their families.
Malaysians in the affected areas, as well as family members with relevant information, may contact the ministry through the following channels:
Ministry Of Foreign Affairs Operations Room
Phone number: +603 8887 4570
E-mail:
dutyofficer@kln.gov.my
The ministry urged the public not to speculate or share unverified information while efforts to establish the safety and whereabouts of the Malaysians concerned remain ongoing.
“Further updates will be provided based on verified information received through official channels,” said the ministry, noting that it continues to monitor developments closely. — Bernama

Title: Nearly RM250,000 payout after Segambut jogger fractures spine while fending off neighbour’s German Shepherds
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 29 — The owner of two German Shepherds has been ordered to pay nearly RM250,000 in damages after his neighbour fractured his spine while trying to protect himself from the dogs during a jogging incident five years ago.
Sinar Harian
reported that KL Sessions Court judge Zawiyah Saad found Datuk Seri Ong Thiam Boon liable for the February 10, 2021 incident involving his neighbour, Datuk Mohd Kamal Abdullah.
The court awarded Mohd Kamal RM178,457.60 in special damages and RM70,000 in general damages after a full trial.
Zawiyah reached the decision after considering witness testimony, documentary evidence and written submissions from both sides.
Ong was also ordered to pay interest of 5 per cent a year on the damages from the date of judgment until full settlement.
The court dismissed his counterclaim with costs and ordered him to pay a further RM15,000 in costs to Mohd Kamal.
In his lawsuit, Mohd Kamal alleged that two German Shepherds belonging to Ong attacked him while he was jogging at Taman Anjung Tiara in Segambut.
He said he fell while trying to protect himself from the dogs, fracturing his spine and later requiring surgery and follow-up treatment.
Mohd Kamal alleged that the incident was caused by Ong’s failure to properly control the animals and to ensure that the gate to his home remained closed.
Ong, however, denied that the dogs had attacked or even come into contact with Mohd Kamal.
According to his defence, Mohd Kamal lost his balance and fell while moving backwards on a steep and uneven road after swinging a walking stick at the two dogs.
Ong also argued that Mohd Kamal’s injuries were caused or contributed to by his own negligence.
In a counterclaim, Ong alleged that Mohd Kamal had threatened him, causing fear, humiliation and mental distress.
Mohd Kamal was represented by lawyer Shahril Madisa of Messrs Shahrul Hamidi & Haziq, while Ong was represented by Tan Shao Jia and Wong Win Xien of Messrs Manjit Singh Sachdev, Mohammad Radzi & Partners.

Title: Pakatan open to Bersatu tie-up for Melaka state election as Amirudin says ‘that is politics’
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 29 — Pakatan Harapan (PH) is open to working with Parti Pribumi Bersatu Malaysia in the coming Melaka state election, Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari said, signalling that even former political adversaries could become potential partners as parties manoeuvre ahead of the polls.
The
New Straits Times
reported that the PH election director said the coalition had no objection to considering cooperation with Bersatu or other parties if circumstances required it and if such an arrangement could help ensure political stability.
“Bersatu? If we can accept working with Umno, surely, we can accept Bersatu.
“For example, we previously worked with Umno, and before that, we worked with Bersatu.
“Then there was the Sheraton Move. PAS has also worked with Bersatu, PAS has separated from Bersatu, PAS has separated from Umno, and PAS has wanted to work with Umno. That is politics,” Amirudin told reporters after officiating the Madani Kita programme with the Ampang Jaya community today.
His remarks come amid increasingly fluid negotiations over the Melaka election, with PH and Barisan Nasional (BN) expected to discuss electoral cooperation while PAS has also reportedly held preliminary talks with Umno.
Bersatu, however, was reportedly excluded from those PAS-Umno discussions.
Amirudin, who is also Selangor menteri besar, suggested the shifting alliances need not necessarily be seen as a sign of political instability.
“If people see this as political uncertainty, then it is political uncertainty.
“But if people see it as a new form of political maturity, it could change Malaysia’s political landscape,” he said.
He said PH remained united and had previously shown that it was prepared to make compromises with other parties, including allowing BN to contest seats in Selangor that had previously been won by PH.
Amirudin said PH would prepare for various possibilities in Melaka while ensuring that cooperation within the coalition remained intact.
Any prospective alliance, he said, would have to be based on sincerity and a clear commitment to preserving the stability and prosperity achieved under the unity government.
He also invoked the political turmoil that followed the Sheraton Move in 2020, which led to the collapse of the then PH federal government.
“We do not want to repeat that, and we need to establish a stable government,” he said.
Amirudin has been tasked with handling possible electoral cooperation between PH and BN in Melaka.
The current Melaka state assembly’s term expires at the end of December, with an election required within 60 days of its dissolution.
BN chairman Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi has previously said the coalition intends to defend all 21 seats it won in the 2021 Melaka election, while remaining open to electoral cooperation.
BN won 21 of the state assembly’s 28 seats in that election, while PH secured five and Perikatan Nasional (PN) two.
PAS president Tan Sri Abdul Hadi Awang has meanwhile said PN would drop cooperation with BN if BN chose to contest alongside PH.

Title: BNM warns of scammers using phone numbers similar to STR, Sara hotlines and impersonating MoF officials
Article:
KUCHING, Aug 29 — Members of the public have been advised to remain vigilant against individuals impersonating officials from the Sumbangan Tunai Rahmah (STR) and Sumbangan Asas Rahmah (Sara) programmes.
Bank Negara Malaysia (BNM), in issuing the warning, said some criminal groups had resorted to using telephone numbers similar to official hotlines to contact members of the public and gain their trust before obtaining their personal and banking information.
“Some individuals are impersonating officials from the Ministry of Finance (MoF), claiming to represent the STR and Sara programmes, and contacting people using numbers similar to official phone numbers in an attempt to trick victims into providing personal information,” said BNM in a Facebook post.
BNM reminded all that the MoF has not authorised any third party to use its official contact numbers to handle STR or Sara matters, and that MoF officials would never ask the public to make any payments on their behalf.
The central bank appealed to the public not to disclose any personal or banking information to unidentified callers, including their MyKad number, bank account number, One-Time Password (OTP) or Transaction Authorisation Code (TAC), online banking password or Personal Identification Number (PIN), and other personal and financial information.
It also urged the public to adhere to the ‘3S’ anti-fraud principle: Soal (inquire), Sekat (block) and Sebar (share).
The public must first inquire about and verify the information and identity provided by the caller; subsequently, they must never provide personal or banking information to strangers; and lastly, they should inform friends and family about the scam and report it to the enforcement authorities to help prevent more people from falling prey to scammers.
“If a person unfortunately falls victim to fraud, he/she should immediately contact his/her bank’s hotline to request assistance in blocking suspicious transactions.
“The victim should also call the National Scam Response Centre (NSRC) at 997 for assistance and report the incident to the police for further investigation,” pointed out BNM.
The central bank also advised the public to immediately end any suspicious call claiming to be from officials of the STR or SARA programmes.
They should then contact the relevant authorities through official channels to verify the caller’s identity and the information provided.
