Title: Printer apologises, says last-minute order led to incorrect Jalur Gemilang star worn by Kedah MB
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 29 — A printing company has blamed a rushed last-minute order and less thorough quality checks for an incorrect Jalur Gemilang star appearing on attire worn by Kedah Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Muhammad Sanusi Md Nor and several dignitaries at a Merdeka event.
Berita Harian
reported that NE Creative Ventures has apologised publicly to the Kedah Menteri Besar’s Office and accepted full responsibility for the mistake, after photographs of the attire went viral on social media.
The Ayer Keroh, Melaka-based company said an error during production resulted in the star on the printed Malaysian flag having fewer than the official 14 points.
“The design of the attire was printed based on the reference artwork file received before undergoing a technical tracing process during the production stage.
“We acknowledge that an oversight occurred after receiving an additional last-minute order to meet a tight deadline, resulting in the detailed checking process, or quality control, being less thorough,” the company said in an official letter to the Menteri Besar’s Office that was sighted by the national daily.
The company said it would immediately provide replacement attire that complied with the official specifications of the Jalur Gemilang.
It also said it took public criticism over the viral images seriously and would tighten its standard operating procedures, particularly for products featuring official symbols, state crests or corporate logos.
“We deeply regret any inconvenience caused and greatly appreciate the cooperation and tolerance shown by all parties involved.
“From today, the company will require customers to sign a final artwork approval form before any printing process, especially for items involving official symbols, state crests or corporate logos,” it said.
Pictures of Sanusi and several dignitaries wearing the attire drew criticism online after social media users noticed that the star on the Jalur Gemilang did not have the required 14 points.
The photographs were first published by Warta Kedah, the Kedah state government’s official media channel, before being widely shared on social media.
The clothing was worn during the Merdeka Kibar Jalur Gemilang Boat Parade yesterday, held in conjunction with Malaysia’s 69th Independence Day celebrations.
The event was jointly organised by the Anak Bukit and Suka Menanti state constituency service centres and officiated by Sanusi.
Nearly 100 boats took part in the parade from Kampung Alor Madi to the State Museum while flying the Jalur Gemilang.

Title: Parents must caution teens that mule accounts can lead to legal action, says Ewon
Article:
PENAMPANG, Aug 29 — Parents should educate and remind their children, particularly teenagers, not to become involved in mule account syndicates, which could expose them to legal action.
Sabah Deputy Chief Minister III Datuk Ewon Benedick, who is also Industrial Development, Entrepreneurship and Transport Minister, said allowing others to use their bank accounts could expose account holders to legal action if the accounts were found to have been used for fraud or other unlawful transactions.
“This is something we need to pay attention to. We need to remind ourselves, parents and children, especially teenagers, not to be easily deceived or allow their accounts to be used by others.
“Digital technology is now part of our daily lives. Therefore, while making use of technology, we also need to understand the risks and threats that come with it,” he said at the Digital Parenting Programme Series IV for the Kapayan state constituency, organised by the National Population and Family Development Board (LPPKN), here today.
Ewon, who is also Penampang Member of Parliament, said digital technology had changed how people carried out various activities, including financial transactions, business dealings and applications for government assistance.
He said QR code payments were also becoming increasingly common, including among traders at markets, showing that digital transactions were now part of everyday life.
“The same applies to the various entrepreneurship grants available nationwide. Many grant applications for entrepreneurs, associations and cooperatives, including those provided by the federal government, are now submitted online.
“However, the use of digital technology needs to be balanced so that people, especially young people, do not become too focused on their smartphones and neglect their responsibilities and other important aspects of life,” he said.
On the programme, Ewon expressed hope that the sharing sessions would enhance parents’ knowledge and help them guide their children in using digital technology safely, responsibly and wisely.
“I will continue to support parenting initiatives like this, which not only benefit the community but also remind me of my own responsibilities as a father,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Amirudin tells Umno to ‘look in the mirror’ over sincerity in election seat talks
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 29 — PKR election director Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari has pushed back against Umno’s call for sincerity in future election negotiations, saying Barisan Nasional (BN) should first examine its own approach after Pakatan Harapan (PH) previously gave up seats it had won to accommodate its unity government partner.
Utusan Malaysia
reported that Amirudin said negotiations would become difficult if one side imposed conditions before discussions had even begun.
He said PH had already demonstrated its willingness to compromise during previous state elections, including by allowing BN to contest constituencies in Selangor that had been won by PKR.
“We negotiated sincerely during the state elections, and we hope there will be the same sincerity when we hold discussions elsewhere. So remember, in Johor and Selangor, we sincerely gave way even in constituencies that we had won.
“Don’t impose conditions before discussions have even begun. If you say you will only contest seats that were lost, that makes things difficult. In Selangor, we gave BN seats that we had won.
“So when it comes to sincerity, you also have to look at yourself in the mirror. We are open to discussions, but everyone has to be sincere,” he told the national daily after officiating the Madani Kita programme with the Ampang Jaya community today.
His remarks came a day after Umno secretary-general Datuk Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki said any negotiations with other parties over cooperation in the coming election must be based on sincerity and trust rather than threats or intimidation.
Amirudin, who is also Selangor menteri besar, said PH remained open to negotiating seat allocations, including constituencies beyond the 21 seats identified by Umno and BN.
“Those are indeed seats that we should consider [apart from the 21 seats]. But we will see how the discussions go. We have not even started discussions yet, so I do not want to get ahead of myself.
“But the point is that there has to be sincerity. We have negotiated sincerely before. We were even willing to share constituencies that we had won,” he said.
Amirudin also said he had been in contact with Melaka Chief Minister Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh, but was waiting for him to be ready to begin formal discussions.
“Rauf explained that he is waiting for several policy decisions at the Umno central and BN central levels before proceeding with discussions and so on,” he said.
Asked why PH was still prepared to work with BN despite BN having previously been described as “sakau”, a Malay term commonly used to suggest corruption or the plundering of public funds, Amirudin said such criticism had been directed at individuals rather than the party as a whole.
“It referred to individuals and not to an entire party, and we have the federal level to consider. That is why we have never said that we must work with Umno.
“We have to be prepared to cooperate with various parties. When Umno says it is willing to cooperate, okay, then we discuss it. If we were to take that view [of the entire party], we would already have changed the situation at the federal level,” he said.

Title: Desa ParkCity deaths: Post-mortems show two children were stabbed in the neck, mother suffered sharp-force wounds, says KL police chief
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 29 — Two children found dead with their parents at a Desa ParkCity home were killed by stab wounds to the neck, post-mortem examinations have confirmed.
Berita Harian
reported that Kuala Lumpur police chief Datuk Fadil Marsus said their mother, 47, meanwhile, died from sharp-force trauma to the neck and chest.
The findings provide the clearest account yet of how three members of the family died, as police continue investigating whether a suspected love scam and debts totalling RM260,000 were linked to the killings.
Fadil said the post-mortem on the couple’s nine-year-old daughter was carried out at the National Institute of Forensic Medicine at Kuala Lumpur Hospital yesterday.
The examination began at 9am and ended at noon.
“The post-mortem found that the cause of death was a stab wound to the neck,” he said.
The mother’s post-mortem began at about 2pm and was completed at 7.30pm.
“The post-mortem found that the cause of death was sharp-force trauma to the neck and chest,” Fadil said.
The couple’s seven-year-old son was also examined yesterday, with the post-mortem running from 2pm to 5pm.
“The post-mortem found that the victim died from a stab wound to the neck,” he said.
Fadil said the post-mortem on the children’s father, 48, described by police as the suspect, would be carried out today after examinations at the scene were completed.
“The post-mortem is expected to begin at 2pm and be completed at about 6pm today.
“All four bodies have yet to be claimed and will only be claimed after the post-mortem on the suspect has been completed,” he said.
He added that forensic personnel from HKL and the Royal Malaysia Police were at the home to carry out further examinations.
Police are also investigating claims surrounding a note allegedly linked to a love scam, including losses and debts amounting to RM260,000.
Fadil said the matter remained under investigation, but added that the family was aware of the love-scam issue and that the wife was believed to have been drawn into an illegal investment scheme.
Yesterday, investigators said they were looking into whether pressure over the RM260,000 debt, after the wife allegedly fell victim to a love scam, could have been a motive for the man to kill his wife and two children before taking his own life.
The speculation followed the discovery of a note believed to have been left by the father on the dining table of the family’s Desa ParkCity home.

Title: Putrajaya comes alive as National Day 2026 full rehearsal gets under way
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Aug 29 — Dataran Putrajaya came alive with uniformed contingents, Jalur Gemilang and the roar of national assets during today’s full rehearsal for the 2026 National Day celebrations.
Beginning at 8 am, the rehearsal provided a preview of Monday’s celebrations, featuring corporate and government-linked companies (GLCs) and colourful special performances.
Patriotic songs and drum performances at the Gema Inovasi Madani special event helped lift the mood among thousands of people who had gathered at Dataran Putrajaya from as early as 6 am.
A Bernama check found that families from various ethnic and social backgrounds brought their children to watch the event as the school holidays began, and stayed until the rehearsal ended at 10 am.
Nurmaizatul Fatihah Hanif, 32, from Kajang, Selangor, said she and her three children had attended to show their support for her younger sibling, who is a student at Universiti Pertahanan Malaysia and is taking part in the giant flag procession.
She said it was the first time her children had seen the parade in person, having watched it only on television in previous years.
“Merdeka Day is always exciting, and watching the parade is something we look forward to. My children were especially excited when they heard the jets during the display, as we usually only see them on television. They were also thrilled to see the cute mascots,” she said.
Meanwhile, Nur Hafizza Mohd Shukri, 24, said the aerial display and K9 unit’s performance had encouraged her to return for the main celebration on Aug 31.
“I’m planning to come back here on Monday and leave home early, so I don’t miss the main events. Hopefully, it will be a lively celebration, with cooler weather and no rain,” she said.
A variety of vibrant performances and creative showcases highlighting Malaysia’s diverse arts and cultural heritage stole the spotlight during today’s full rehearsal for the 2026 National Day celebrations at Dataran Putrajaya August 29, 2026. — Bernama pic
Among the highlights of the 2026 National Day and Malaysia Day (HKHM) rehearsal was a human graphic performance involving 1,500 students from 36 schools in Selangor.
Moving in formations to the music and changing their visuals as contingents passed through the main area, the students created a dynamic display that complemented each segment of the performance.
The display of the country’s defence assets was another highlight, featuring the PT-91M Pendekar 125mm tank, Lipan Bara high-mobility armoured vehicles and Gempita multipurpose amphibious armoured vehicles in various weapon configurations, including 30mm AFV and ATGW variants.
The assets demonstrated the Malaysian Armed Forces’ capabilities and operational readiness in safeguarding national sovereignty.
A total of 10,819 participants will take part in the 2026 HKHM parade and procession, involving 76 contingents, 22 marching bands, 11 decorated vehicles, 328 land, sea, and air assets, and 112 service animals.
More than 80,000 people are expected at the 69th National Day celebrations at Dataran Putrajaya, themed “Malaysia Madani: Kesejahteraan Dinikmati”. — Bernama

Title: Durian, pineapple and RM8b in deals: Malaysia goes big at MAHA 2026
Article:
SERDANG, Aug 29 — Some 121 Memoranda of Understanding (MoUs) worth about RM8 billion are expected to be signed in conjunction with the Malaysia Agriculture, Horticulture and Agrotourism Exhibition (MAHA) 2026 at the Malaysia Agro Exposition Park Serdang (Maeps) here.
Agriculture and Food Security Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Sabu said about RM4 billion of the total would involve partnerships with China, while the remainder would involve other countries.
He said the agreements would cover technology exchange, investment opportunities, capacity building and training for farmers, including Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET), as well as creating opportunities for local agri-food products to enter export markets.
He added that the MAHA Go Global initiative would also help expand the reach of local products, particularly in Central Asia and Eastern Europe.
“That is why, through MAHA Go Global and FAMA, we hope to play a greater role in expanding markets for Malaysian products, particularly in markets where we are still lagging behind,” he told a press conference after officiating MAHA 2026 at Maeps here today.
Also present were his deputy Datuk Chan Foong Hin and the ministry’s secretary-general Datuk Seri Isham Ishak.
Mohamad identified pineapples and durians as among the local products with strong potential for expansion into international markets.
Malaysia’s pineapple exports now exceed RM1 billion, while demand for durians in China remains high, providing room for further growth, he said.
A key focus of MAHA 2026 is value creation, ensuring that local agricultural produce is not only sold as raw commodities but also processed into higher-value downstream products.
The approach is important to prevent the country from exporting raw materials and later importing processed products from overseas, he added.
“We do not want to export raw materials and then import products processed overseas. If possible, we should process them ourselves, so that value creation continues all the way to the end user in Malaysia,” he said.
The agriculture sector has also shown positive growth in its contribution to the country’s Gross Domestic Product (GDP), with the ministry expecting this to increase this year.
Efforts to boost agricultural exports need to be intensified to help balance the country’s agri-food import bill, which currently exceeds RM80 billion.
“We are now increasing our exports. That is what we are working on. Through MAHA, we can step up these efforts,” he said.
MAHA 2026 is being held from August 28 to September 6 at Maeps, featuring about 2,000 exhibitors and targeting more than four million visitors. — Bernama

Title: Jendela Phase Two to begin at 1,000 sites nationwide this year, says deputy minister
Article:
KULAI, Aug 29 — A total of 1,000 sites, including in Sabah and Sarawak, have been identified for the implementation of Phase Two of the National Digital Network (Jendela) plan this year, said Deputy Communications Minister Teo Nie Ching.
She said its implementation would ensure stronger and more stable internet coverage nationwide.
“There are 2,700 sites under the implementation of Jendela Phase Two, but for the first phase (of Phase Two) this year, 1,000 sites have been identified, and the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) has issued tenders for implementation at the sites,” she told a press conference after officiating the Japen@Petronas Jalur Gemilang Expression Programme here today.
Jendela is a government initiative coordinated by MCMC to improve digital infrastructure and internet coverage nationwide.
Meanwhile, Teo said various activities had been lined up for the public through the RIUH Merdeka programme, particularly for those planning to camp out at Dataran Putrajaya to watch the parade.
She said free public transport facilities, including shuttle buses, would also be provided at MRT Putrajaya Sentral every five minutes, while services at the Putrajaya International Convention Centre would operate every 10 minutes.
“Therefore, the public are encouraged to use public transport as many roads will be closed,” she said.
Earlier, Teo, who is also the Kulai Member of Parliament, distributed free Jalur Gemilang-shaped magnets to the public to enliven the National Month celebrations.
She said the initiative was a collaboration between the Communications Ministry, Japen and Petronas at selected petrol stations. — Bernama

Title: More than 2,300 police deployed for National Day celebrations in Putrajaya
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Aug 29 — A total of 2,354 members and officers of the Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM) have been assigned to ensure the highest level of security and smooth running of the 2026 National Day celebrations at Dataran Putrajaya on Monday.
Putrajaya district police chief ACP Aidi Sham Mohamed said the assignment involved static control and traffic control at strategic locations in the area where the annual event is being held.
“For the public, I advise them to come early to Dataran Putrajaya and comply with all the regulations of the authorities.
“This includes not parking vehicles in prohibited places, not blocking traffic, and at the same time, take care of your own safety, especially the safety of children and belongings,” he said.
He told reporters after the full rehearsal of the 2026 National Day celebration attended by Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil here today.
Aidi Sham also reminded the public not to bring any dangerous weapons when attending the National Day celebration.
“Do not bring any dangerous weapons for the purpose of enlivening our National Day this year,” he said.
Earlier, Fahmi said the 2026 National Day celebration at Dataran Putrajaya on August 31, will so far be held as usual,
Themed “
Malaysia Madani: Kesejahteraan Dinikmati
”, the 69th National Day celebration will be held at Dataran Putrajaya with an expectation of more 80,000 visitors coming to witness the historic day. — Bernama

Title: Fire destroys 60pc of Pos Laju building in Bekenu, no injuries reported
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 29 — A fire destroyed about 60 per cent of a Pos Laju building in Bekenu, about 47km south-west of Miri in Sarawak, this morning, although no one was injured.
The Sarawak Fire and Rescue Department’s Operations Centre said in a statement today that it received an emergency call at 8.44am before five firefighters from the Batu Niah Fire and Rescue Station were dispatched to the scene.
The team, led by Senior Fire Officer II Azalan Azaman, arrived at about 9.30am and found the Pos Laju building, measuring about 15.2m by 12.2m, on fire.
“Initial inspections found that an estimated 60 per cent of the permanent structure had been destroyed by the fire.
“No victims were reported to have been involved or injured in the incident,” the department said.
Firefighters battled the blaze using a hose line stretching about 122m with two nozzles, while also drawing water from an open source.
The fire was brought under control at about 9.58am, while extinguishing and follow-up operations continued at the scene.
A Compact Rescue Tender and five firefighters were deployed for the operation.
The cause of the fire and the estimated losses have yet to be determined.
